## 昨日提交分析（第 1/1 批，共 3 条）

### 1. 主要更新类型
以 **Bug 修复** 和 **功能新增** 为主，兼顾 **CI/运维配置** 调整：
- 2 条修复：NPU 计算单元读取错误、GDN 反向传播 NaN
- 1 条功能：新增模型迁移技能与 HunyuanVideo 1.5 模型支持

### 2. 关键变更点及其与项目方向的关系
- **[542cd89] NPU 计算单元读取修复（ops, ci）**：将计算单元（compute units）来源从 CPU 线程数改为实际读取 NPU 设备参数。这直接服务于项目"以模型为中心的分布式训练配方库"的目标——分布式并行配置（如 TP/DP 划分）需要准确的硬件拓扑信息，用 CPU 线程数近似 NPU 参数会导致并行策略配置不当。
- **[4f7808b] GDN 反向 NaN 修复 + fla_npu v26.10.0 升级（ops）**：针对 Ascend950 上 Gated Delta Network 反向传播产生 NaN 的问题，同时迁移到新版 NPU 原生 fla 内核。这体现了项目对国产 NPU 后端（昇腾）持续适配的投入。
- **[edd04cc] 模型迁移技能 + HunyuanVideo 1.5（agent, model）**：新增 "model migration skill"（模型迁移技能）和混元视频 1.5 模型，扩展了项目的多模态模型覆盖范围（视频模态），并引入了辅助迁移的工具/Agent 能力。

### 3. 对项目的影响和潜在意义
- **稳定性提升**：两条修复分别解决了分布式配置错误和训练数值不稳定（NaN）两个严重问题，对在 NPU 环境下大规模训练的可靠性至关重要——NaN 问题若不修复会导致整批训练任务作废。
- **硬件生态深化**：连续两条提交聚焦 NPU（昇腾），表明项目正加速国产算力适配，降低对单一硬件平台的依赖。
- **模态扩展**：HunyuanVideo 1.5 的加入延续了项目"Any Modality"的愿景，从语言/图像进一步覆盖视频生成模态。
- **迁移工具化**：模型迁移技能的引入暗示项目希望降低新模型接入成本，与 README 中 "Recipe Zoo"（配方库）的理念一致——让配方的编写和迁移更自动化。

### 4. 值得关注的技术点
- **compute units 语义陷阱**：分布式训练中用 CPU 线程数替代 NPU 计算单元是一种常见的隐式假设，此类修复提醒开发者在异构硬件下需显式查询设备拓扑。
- **GDN + Ascend950 的数值稳定性**：GDN 类线性注意力变体的反向传播在特定硬件上出现 NaN，可能涉及内核精度（FP16/BF16）或梯度累加的硬件差异，值得深入排查。
- ** fla_npu 版本迁移**：fla（linear attention）内核从旧版迁到 v26.10.0，说明 NPU 生态的内核库在快速迭代，版本对齐是保持性能与正确性的关键。
- **"模型迁移技能"抽象**：以 skill 形式封装迁移逻辑，可能对应可复用的 prompt/工具链，是 LLM 辅助开发在框架维护中的实际应用。

### 5. 对项目发展的整体影响
结合 README 中 "Scaling Any Modality Model Training" 的项目定位，这批提交从三个维度推进了项目：**硬件维度**（深化 NPU 适配、修复关键数值 bug，保障大规模训练可行）、**模态维度**（新增视频模型，兑现 Any Modality 承诺）、**工程维度**（CI 配置修正和迁移技能，提升配方库的可维护性与可扩展性）。这些变更共同强化了项目作为"分布式多模态训练配方库"的核心竞争力——即在多样化硬件和模态上提供稳定、可复现的训练方案。

# FlashInfer 昨日提交合并总结（共 81 个提交）

## 一、主要更新类型
以性能优化为绝对主体（约八成），覆盖注意力（FMHA、分页/DSA 稀疏、GQA、KDA）、GEMM 与 LM Head、门控 Delta 规则 GDN、RMSNorm/SiLU 门控 RMSNorm、因果卷积、SwiGLU 量化、MoE 解码、MoK、mHC 等核心算子，并明确区分确定性与非确定性双轨实现；其余为关键 Bug 修复（竞态、数值污染、CI 回归、新平台兼容）、功能新增（GDN 树形投机解码、KDA fp32 状态、MoE 自动配置、Prims-TS 路由 FP8 32×32 块尺度权重），以及测试重组、CI 加固与文档完善等工程卫生改动。

## 二、关键变更
- **训练内核系统性补齐**：MoE 分组 GEMM 权重梯度、RMSNorm 与 LM Head 训练反向、GDN 反向、因果卷积 KCP 反向、DSA indexer 等逐硬件（sm_100a/103a/107a、Hopper）逐 shape 调优，收益多为 1.01–1.5×，个别达 2.4×，普遍承诺逐位一致。
- **GDN 树形投机解码**：新增 `verify_parents` 与 `accept_paths`，基于 staged 位置的路径无关递推打破连续前缀假设，`HAS_PATHS=False` 变体与原 kernel 位级一致，per-token 解码延迟降 3–27%，解锁 SGLang/vLLM 树形 MTP。
- **MoE 自动调优**：`MoEEpLayer` 引入 AutoConfig 在 Mega/Split 配置间自动择优；CuBLASLt 策略由启发式索引改为算法描述符，修复 autotuner 桶边界失效。
- **推理侧精进**：tiny-KV 扩展到 FP8 Q/KV 与 1–3 query token（batch 64 提速 3.8×）、NVFP4 分页注意力辅助 warp 解量化、masked 批量 GEMM 预取、LatentMoE TP8 尾部路由重调（1.07–1.38×）。
- **Bug 修复**：KDA 共享内存缺 fence 致 TMA 竞态（TensorRT-LLM 实测 590/1000 脏写入）、跨 CTA 屏障改集群作用域、top-k fast-math 刷零 denormal 加 `--ftz=false`、注意力尾块 0×NaN 污染整 tile、DSA 梯度缓存键不完整、`kser` 非确定性规划回归、checkpoint 显存超额预留（GB200 每卡省 8942 MiB）、跨 stream/CUDA graph 事件驱动缓存协议消除竞态、修复 132 个 CPU 测试回归。
- **硬件与生态**：解除 SM107（Rubin）对 DeepSeek fp8 32×32 scale 门控，修复 NVFP4/BF16 分区 MoE 兼容，为 Kimi-K3 等新模型提供即插即用加速。

## 三、项目影响
FlashInfer 正从单一推理库演进为**推理与训练统一、横跨 Blackwell 与 Rubin 多代架构的生产级 GPU 内核基础设施**。KCP 卷积反向较 FLA、Megatron-Core、torch.compile 快 2.05–2.25×；GDN 解码 host 时间提升 1.22–1.25×、CUDA graph 时间最高 1.38×、kernel 时间 geomean 1.08×。分段 FP32 梯度累加器与私有 MemPool 压低峰值内存，确定性与内存稳定性成为差异化卖点；提交普遍附带 A/A 噪声带、bootstrap 置信区间及与 cuDNN、FLA、FlashQLA、trtllm-gen、DeepGEMM、Triton 的逐形状对比，为后续高吞吐 PR 合并与 v0.7.4 发布铺路。

## 四、技术关注点
优化以调度级为主而非算术级：最后 CTA 延迟等待、高优先级侧流并行主机准备、masked_m 预取省去 CTA 同步、长行 look-ahead 预取、KCP"主启动 + 后置修补"隐藏 halo 交换延迟、空闲 warp 参与 V 解量化、CTA 双 query head 打包使因果对角线冗余从 15.2% 降至 9.3%、单 4-CTA cluster 内 split-K 按序累加服务瘦权重梯度、queue-walk 动态认领兼顾负载均衡与逐位可复现、masked 索引 `-2 - (CTA % 128)` 借 TMA 零填充消除 L2 热点、fp64 参考实现作为验证锚点并修复分叉被静默当链处理（0.556 相对误差）。特别注意 0×NaN 陷阱需在共享内存显式清零尾部 V 行，且非确定性路线仅在 `dweight` 放弃逐位一致、其余保持一致。后续值得关注 sm_107a 路由是否推广到更多算子，以及 KCP 训练内核确定性版本能否补齐。

## 📌 Description

Four `tests/cpu` files fail on `main`: 132 tests on the scheduled H100
run
([42620412926](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/42620412926)),
on both the current and the new CI image. In each file a test stub or
heuristic did not follow a library change that merged on a targeted run
without `tests/cpu`. The library code is unchanged; only the tests are
fixed.

| Fails on main | Test file | Broken by | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 125 (124 in setup) |
`tests/cpu/cake/test_cake_kcp_partition_parity.py` | #9155 | The alias
guard in `_entry` rejected any public function naming `kcp` and
`partition`, so the new exported `kcp_partition_digest` helper failed
the check. A name now counts as an alias only when all its other words
are package-name words (`cake`, `kda`, `gdn`, `det`, `nondet`, `train`,
`kcp`). `partition_det_kcp` and similar old names are still rejected. |
| 4 | `tests/cpu/prims_ts/test_moe_runner_ffi_tensors.py` | #8666 | The
two stub `Config` classes set `use_deepseek_fp8 = 0`, the real config's
default, which `_validate_swap_ab_out_hidden` now reads. |
| 1 | `tests/cpu/prims_ts/test_batched_gemm_captured_schedule_tasks.py`
| #8666 | The stub resource's `mma()` takes `k_subblock:
Constexpr[Optional[int]] = None`, matching the real `TmemC.mma`
signature. |
| 2 | `tests/cpu/attention/test_cudnn_prepared_contract.py` | #8590 |
The wrapper built with `__new__` sets `_batch_invariant = None` (the
`__init__` default), which `reset_workspace_buffer()` now reads. |

## 🔍 Related Issues

Breaks introduced by #9155, #8666 and #8590. They block #6266 (Docker CI
tag update), whose full run fails only on these tests plus one tolerance
flake.

### [a0a3323](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a0a3323a68460b9d6b8c28259e1be528be6974fd)

- **作者**: feih-nv
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T22:26:27Z
- **提交信息**: fix(moe): read the activation-matrix doc as UTF-8 (#9237)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re
needed. -->

`scripts/generate_moe_activation_matrix.py` reads and rewrites
`docs/design_docs/flashinfer_moe_api.md` with `Path.read_text()` /
`Path.write_text()` and no encoding. On native Windows the locale
encoding is cp1252, and the UTF-8 design doc contains bytes cp1252
cannot decode, so
`tests/cpu/moe/test_unified_moe_activation_matrix.py::test_documented_activation_matrix_matches_runner_registry`
raises `UnicodeDecodeError` (NVBug 7058649). Linux is unaffected because
its locale is UTF-8.

Read the doc as UTF-8. Write it back as UTF-8 with `newline="\n"` so
Windows does not rewrite the checked-in LF file as CRLF. `read_text()`
accepts those CRLF bytes, so the next check would still pass; the
rewrite dirties the worktree when Git is not normalizing line endings.

### [c1eed07](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c1eed07c0edd967b7333b3045f611065e194cc15)

- **作者**: Ka-Hyun Nam
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T21:24:56Z
- **提交信息**: feat(kda): fp32 state for the CuTe recurrent decode kernels (#8833)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`recurrent_kda`'s CuTe DSL decode kernels (one-warp and grouped)
hardcoded a bf16 state, so the fp32 state pools that the serving
frameworks use were rejected: a launcher `ValueError` before #6893, a
`TypeError` since. This makes both kernels follow the state dtype (bf16
or fp32), read and written back in its own dtype. The math was already
fp32 in registers; only the staging registers, the compile fakes and the
compile cache keys were bf16-specific. `initial_state_source` must match
the state dtype; any other dtype still raises `TypeError`.

The T=1 unpacked fast path and the Cake selector still require bf16 and
decline fp32, so fp32 falls through to the one-warp or grouped kernel.
`backend="cake"` and `packed_kda_decode` remain bf16-only (the fused
decode ops already accept bf16 or fp32); the docs note says so.

Tests: new `tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda_fp32_state.py` (fp32 output and
final state against an fp32 reference in packed and batched layouts at
H=16/64 and HV>H, covering the grouped and one-warp routes; untouched
pool rows bit-identical; state not rounded to bf16; fp16 rejected;
multi-token spec decode with an fp32 pool against a sequential fp32
reference, with and without `num_accepted_tokens`; bf16 then fp32 then
bf16 in one process to pin the compile cache keys). The two tests that
pinned the fp32 `TypeError` (#6893, #8052) are replaced.

fp32 cost, `recurrent_kda` packed `[1, B]` + `cu_seqlens` +
`ssm_state_indices`, H=HV=64, K=V=128, T=1, precomputed gate, GB300
(SM103), CUPTI with cold L2, 5 interleaved rounds x 20 iterations,
clocks not locked, microseconds (FLA = vLLM's
`fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule` called the same way):

| B | FI bf16 | FI fp32 (new support added by this PR) | FLA bf16 | FLA
fp32 | FI fp32 / FLA fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.2 | 4.3 | 5.5 | 7.1 | 0.61x |
| 8 | 10.0 | 14.1 | 13.1 | 19.9 | 0.71x |
| 32 | 30.8 | 45.8 | 37.9 | 63.3 | 0.72x |
| 128 | 111.6 | 172.3 | 148.4 | 234.8 | 0.73x |

bf16 is unchanged by this PR: upstream main against this branch on
GB300, same benchmark, two interleaved passes of 5 rounds each,
microseconds, main / branch: B=1 3.22-3.25 / 3.23, B=8 9.89-9.92 /
9.90-9.97, B=32 30.96-30.98 / 30.90-30.98, B=128 111.92-111.97 /
111.95-111.98 (differences under 1%, inside run-to-run spread).

fp32 state costs 1.35-1.54x over bf16 (twice the state bytes) and stays
faster than the FLA kernel on an fp32 pool at every batch size. B200
gives the same ordering (0.63-0.69x).

## 🔍 Related Issues

Addresses the fp32-state item of #6560. The batched `[B, 1]` +
`ssm_state_indices` routing and the 16/64-head docstrings for the fused
ops are not part of this PR.

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re
needed. -->

PRs touching `tests/cpu/` or `tests/test_helpers/` currently causes
confusion in codeownership requirements. This moves the per-op content
next to the op's tests so the existing `tests/<op>/` CODEOWNERS rules
cover it.

No test logic changes:

1. `tests/cpu/<op>/` keeps its layout so CPU-only runners can target one
tree, and CODEOWNERS now gives each `tests/cpu/<op>/` subtree the same
owners as the op's `tests/<op>/` rule. The build/CI/package-level tests
move to `tests/cpu/infra/`, the Cake causal conv1d training tests to
`tests/cpu/causal_conv1d/`.
2. `tests/test_helpers/` is retired. Single-op helpers ->
`tests/<op>/test_helpers/` (attention, comm, utils, moe, kda, norm,
quantization, diffusion_ops, gdn, moe_ep, jit); test-infrastructure
helpers (`parametrize`, `fuzz_ledger`, `cake_profiler`, `cake_package`,
`cake_mode_names`) -> `tests/infra/test_helpers/`; experimental
Cake/Qwen references and fixtures -> `tests/experimental/test_helpers/`.

Also updated: root `conftest.py` plugin path,
`scripts/check_cake_build_manifests.py`, benchmark imports, labeler
globs, csrc READMEs and docs paths, and CODEOWNERS
(`tests/test_helpers/` rule dropped; `tests/infra/` and
`tests/cpu/infra/` take the infra owners;
`tests/utils/test_helpers/sampling.py` joins the sampling rule).
`pytest.ini` already skips any `test_helpers` directory by basename, so
nothing new is collected.

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

FlashInfer's ReplaySSM verify kernel for GDN assumes the draft tokens it
verifies form a contiguous prefix. Tree-structured speculative decoding
(EAGLE-2/3 with `topk > 1`) gives each verified token its own
root-to-node path instead, so SGLang refuses FlashInfer's GDN kernels
whenever tree drafting is on and falls back to Triton, and vLLM has no
tree speculative decode for linear attention at all. This PR adds an
optional `verify_parents` argument, an int32 `[B, T]` parent array, to
the ReplaySSM tcgen05 verify, plus a parent-indexed fp64 reference and
shared test topologies. The parts are separate commits and are
independent of each other.

An SGLang integration behind a flag exists on a fork PR
(kahyunnam/sglang#1) and uses this kernel together with #6257
(accept-path commit): on Qwen3-Next-80B tree MTP it measured 19 to 27
percent lower per-token decode latency at tp=1 and 3 to 10 percent at
tp=4 against SGLang's Triton tree path, with unchanged acceptance and
GSM8K, and drops the per-draft SSM snapshot buffer. The KDA counterpart
that was in earlier revisions of this PR is parked on the fork branch
`kda-tree-verify-parked`: SGLang drives KDA through `recurrent_kda`'s
state-updating mode, which that kernel does not serve, so tree support
for KDA belongs on `recurrent_kda` and will come separately.

### Parent-indexed reference (`tests/gdn/reference_delta_rule.py`,
`tests/test_helpers/spec_tree.py`)

Tree speculative decoding (EAGLE-2/3 with `topk > 1`) gives each draft
token its own root-to-node path instead of the prefix `0..t-1`. The
reference could not say so: fed a fork, it silently returned the chain
answer, which differs from the correct tree answer by a 0.556 relative
error on the forked token with no exception anywhere. SGLang already
gates a tree MTP configuration on a hybrid-GDN model (Qwen3-Next,
`--speculative-eagle-topk 4`) in its registered CI, and that path
currently has no FlashInfer reference coverage at all.

`parents[t]` is the index of token `t`'s parent in the draft, or `-1`
for the initial state, and must be `< t`. The root entry `parents[0]` is
ignored by both kernels, so an engine that writes 0 there (SGLang's conv
kernel does, and rewrites it on every CUDA-graph replay) needs no
sanitizing copy; the opt-in device check accepts -1 or 0 at step 0. It
may be a `[T]` list shared by the batch or an `int [B, T]` tensor per
request. `None` is the chain and leaves the existing path untouched:
with `parents=None` no extra state is allocated, and chain parents `[-1,
0, 1, ...]` are bit-identical to `parents=None` on output, final state
and cached intermediate states. The loop body is unchanged; only the
predecessor state each token continues from is selected per request.

The topology helpers in `tests/test_helpers/spec_tree.py` (six
topologies and the ancestor walk) are imported by both kernel tests
below.

Pure torch, no kernel, no SM gate: the test runs on every CI lane
including CPU-only ones.

### GDN: ReplaySSM tcgen05 verify (`gated_delta_rule_mtp`,
`cache_replayssm=True`)

`gated_delta_rule_mtp` assumes the accepted draft tokens form a
contiguous prefix, so it cannot serve tree-structured drafting
(EAGLE-2/3 with `topk > 1`), where each verified token's history is its
own root-to-node path. SGLang consequently refuses FlashInfer's
linear-attention kernels whenever tree drafting is enabled — in four
separate places, one of which names FlashInfer and tells the operator to
switch backends — and falls back to Triton, which this PR measures at
1.38–5.34x slower than the path added here. In vLLM tree spec decode is
not implemented at all, and `gdn_attn.py` carries a
`num_accepted_tokens: [batch,]` contract with the same prefix assumption
baked in.

This adds an optional `verify_parents` argument, an int32 `[B, T]`
parent array, to the ReplaySSM tcgen05 verify kernel from #5314. When it
is supplied, each output token is computed from its own ancestor set
instead of from the whole prefix. Only the tcgen05 path honors it: if
the call does not qualify for that kernel (SM100/SM103, contiguous fp32
pool with int32 indices, 4 <= T <= 8, B <= 256, K = V = 128, even HV and
HV // H, L2-normalized Q/K), `gated_delta_rule_mtp` raises rather than
silently returning the chain answer from the fp32 fallback.

The reason it belongs on *this* kernel and not on
`gdn_decode_bf16_state` is representational. `gdn_decode_bf16_state`
keeps the state register-resident and updates it in place, reading the
current state at every step, so a tree genuinely needs a distinct state
per node there. The ReplaySSM kernel streams the frozen checkpoint once
and holds the correction as explicit per-token WY factors, so each
staged token's contribution is already a separate term and selecting
ancestors is a selection over terms. Writing `G[i]` for the decay
product along the root→`i` path, the recurrence becomes a weighted sum
over ancestors with `W[j,i] = exp(logG[i] − logG[j])`, and the existing
chain epilogue is already exactly this with `W` folded into an
incrementally rescaled coefficient. Setting `W[j,i] = 0` off the
ancestor set folds the mask into the weight, so the epilogue keeps
`constexpr` loop bounds with no divergence.

`W[j,i] ∈ (0,1]` for ancestors, which is load-bearing rather than
incidental: the alternative factorisation that carries `delta_j / G[j]`
directly reaches `7.97e38` at depth 16 and overflows fp32.

The change is a `logG` parent scan plus a `T×T` weight matrix, both
computed by warp 2, which is otherwise idle between the phase-1 barrier
and the Gram block it already owns. No new barrier is needed — the
`cute.arch.barrier()` that already precedes the epilogue supplies the
SMEM visibility — so the precompute overlaps the state TMA and warp 1's
MMA. SMEM cost is 672 B beside the existing 1 KB Gram matrix. The Gram
matrices, the `r_base` MMA, and the launch shape are untouched, and the
chain path is retained verbatim behind a `constexpr` so chain decoding
is bit-identical and pays nothing.

## Performance

### GDN

Two things have to hold: the existing chain path must not regress, and
the tree path must beat the Triton tree path SGLang falls back to today.
Both measured on a B200, CUDA-event timed under graph replay.

**The chain path does not regress.** `verify_parents=None` compiles a
separate cache entry and the epilogue is retained verbatim, so this is a
check rather than a question:

| batch | chain, before | chain, after | tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 267.95 µs | 268.04 µs | 268.02 µs |
| 1024 | 522.46 µs | 522.42 µs | 522.63 µs |
| 2048 | 1032.59 µs | 1032.38 µs | 1032.61 µs |

**Trees beat the Triton tree path by 1.38–5.34x.** Both sides are handed
the raw gate inputs (`A_log`, `a`, `dt_bias`) and compute the gate
in-kernel, so neither is charged for work the other skips. Triton is
additionally given the `intermediate_states_buffer` its tree path
requires in order to load each node's parent state; the ReplaySSM path
needs no such buffer, so the memory comparison is separately in its
favour.

| B | T | HV | HK | Triton tree | FI chain (prod) | FI RSSM chain | FI
RSSM tree | Triton / FI tree |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 8 | 8 | 2 | 29.0 µs | 18.8 µs | 10.7 µs | 12.6 µs | **2.30x** |
| 32 | 8 | 32 | 8 | 110.8 µs | 76.5 µs | 22.9 µs | 22.9 µs | **4.84x** |
| 128 | 8 | 8 | 2 | 111.4 µs | 76.9 µs | 20.7 µs | 23.4 µs | **4.76x** |
| 512 | 8 | 8 | 2 | 385.2 µs | 233.5 µs | 276.1 µs | 278.2 µs |
**1.38x** |
| 512 | 4 | 8 | 2 | 209.4 µs | 127.4 µs | 141.6 µs | 141.3 µs |
**1.48x** |
| 128 | 8 | 32 | 8 | 385.0 µs | 234.4 µs | 71.4 µs | 72.0 µs | **5.34x**
|

One qualification on tree-versus-chain at small shapes. By per-kernel
CUPTI time on B200 (cold L2, three interleaved passes), the tree path is
1.00 to 1.02x the chain path at `B=32, HV=8` and 1.02 to 1.03x at `B=13,
HV=8`, where the kernel is about 11 µs and the warp-2 precompute no
longer hides entirely under the state TMA; CUDA-graph replay timing at
that size is bimodal and not quotable as a ratio. The claim is at most
2.5 percent above chain by kernel time at `B <= 32`, and within noise at
`B >= 128`.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script
(<code>bench_tree_vs_triton.py</code>)</summary>

The `sglang` package chain is stubbed with real `__path__` values so the
Triton module's intra-package imports resolve without executing sglang's
`__init__`, and `sglang.srt.utils.common` is stubbed down to the single
symbol `fla/utils.py` needs, because the real module pulls in the whole
serving stack.

```python
"""Criterion 2: is FlashInfer's tree verify faster than SGLang's Triton tree verify?

Extends bench_production_bf16.py (which compared FlashInfer *chain* against Triton
tree) with the ReplaySSM tcgen tree path from the proto-tree-verify-mask branch, so
the tree-vs-tree comparison is like-for-like.

Both sides are given the raw gate inputs (A_log, a, dt_bias) and compute the gate
in-kernel, and both are CUDA-event timed under graph replay. Triton additionally
gets a bf16 `intermediate_states_buffer`, which its tree path requires in order to
load each node's parent state; the FlashInfer ReplaySSM path needs no such buffer,
so the memory columns are not comparable in Triton's favour either.
"""

import importlib.util
import sys
import types

import torch

SG = "<path to an sglang checkout>/python"
# Stub the package chain but give each level a real __path__, so the module's
# own intra-package imports (fla.op, fla.utils) resolve without importing
# sglang's heavyweight __init__.
for name in ("sglang", "sglang.srt", "sglang.srt.layers", "sglang.srt.layers.attention",
             "sglang.srt.layers.attention.fla"):
    if name not in sys.modules:
        m = types.ModuleType(name)
        m.__path__ = [f"{SG}/" + name.replace(".", "/")]
        sys.modules[name] = m
# fla.utils wants one symbol from sglang.srt.utils.common, whose real module
# pulls in the whole serving stack. Supply just that symbol.
if "sglang.srt.utils.common" not in sys.modules:
    from packaging import version as _pkgv
    _u = types.ModuleType("sglang.srt.utils"); _u.__path__ = []
    _c = types.ModuleType("sglang.srt.utils.common")
    _c.torch_release = _pkgv.parse(torch.__version__).release
    sys.modules["sglang.srt.utils"] = _u
    sys.modules["sglang.srt.utils.common"] = _c

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "sglang.srt.layers.attention.fla.fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent",
    f"{SG}/sglang/srt/layers/attention/fla/fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent.py")
fr = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules[spec.name] = fr
spec.loader.exec_module(fr)
triton_tree = fr.fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update

from flashinfer.gdn_decode import gated_delta_rule_mtp
from flashinfer.gdn_kernels.gdn_decode_bf16_state import (
    gated_delta_rule_mtp as mtp_bf16,
)

DEV = "cuda"

def make(B, T, HV, HK, K=128, V=128):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    bf = dict(device=DEV, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    slots = B + 2
    return dict(
        q=torch.randn(B, T, HK, K, **bf), k=torch.randn(B, T, HK, K, **bf),
        v=torch.randn(B, T, HV, V, **bf),
        a=torch.randn(B, T, HV, **bf) * 0.5, b=torch.randn(B, T, HV, **bf),
        A_log=torch.randn(HV, device=DEV), dt_bias=torch.randn(HV, device=DEV) * 0.1,
        state=torch.randn(slots, HV, V, K, **bf) * 0.1,
        state_f32=torch.randn(slots, HV, V, K, device=DEV) * 0.1,
        idx=torch.arange(B, device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32),
        ibuf=torch.zeros(B, T, HV, V, K, **bf),
        rawv=torch.zeros(slots, HV, T, V, **bf),
        rawk=torch.zeros(slots, HK, T, K, **bf),
        rg=torch.zeros(slots, HV, T, device=DEV),
        rbeta=torch.zeros(slots, HV, T, device=DEV),
        B=B, T=T, scale=K**-0.5,
    )

def device_us(fn, iters=50, warmup=10):
    for _ in range(warmup):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    s = torch.cuda.Stream(); s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
    with torch.cuda.stream(s):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)
    with torch.cuda.graph(g):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    e0, e1 = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True)
    e0.record()
    for _ in range(iters):
        g.replay()
    e1.record()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return e0.elapsed_time(e1) * 1000.0 / iters

def row(B, T, HV, HK):
    d = make(B, T, HV, HK)
    iidx = torch.arange(B, device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32)
    # Star tree: every node's parent is the root. Satisfies parent[i] < i.
    parent = torch.full((B, T), -1, device=DEV, dtype=torch.int32)
    parent[:, 1:] = 0

    gate = dict(A_log=d["A_log"], a=d["a"], dt_bias=d["dt_bias"],
                softplus_beta=1.0, softplus_threshold=20.0)
    shared = dict(q=d["q"], k=d["k"], v=d["v"], b=d["b"],
                  use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True, scale=d["scale"],
                  disable_state_update=True)

    out = {}
    out["triton_tree"] = device_us(lambda: triton_tree(
        **gate, **shared, is_kda=False,
        initial_state_source=d["state"], initial_state_indices=d["idx"],
        intermediate_states_buffer=d["ibuf"], intermediate_state_indices=iidx,
        cache_steps=T, retrieve_parent_token=parent))

    # Current production FlashInfer path: chain only, cannot take a tree.
    out["fi_chain_prod"] = device_us(lambda: mtp_bf16(
        A_log=d["A_log"].float(), a=d["a"], dt_bias=d["dt_bias"],
        softplus_beta=1.0, softplus_threshold=20.0, **shared,
        initial_state_source=d["state"], initial_state_indices=d["idx"],
        intermediate_states_buffer=d["ibuf"]))

    # ReplaySSM tcgen verify: fp32 checkpoint pool, no snapshot buffer at all.
    rep = dict(A_log=d["A_log"].float(), a=d["a"].float(), dt_bias=d["dt_bias"],
               q=d["q"], k=d["k"], v=d["v"], b=d["b"].float(),
               use_qk_l2norm=True, scale=d["scale"], disable_state_update=True,
               initial_state=d["state_f32"], initial_state_indices=d["idx"],
               cache_replayssm=True, replayssm_rawv=d["rawv"],
               replayssm_rawk=d["rawk"], replayssm_g=d["rg"],
               replayssm_beta=d["rbeta"])
    out["fi_replayssm_chain"] = device_us(lambda: gated_delta_rule_mtp(**rep))
    out["fi_replayssm_tree"] = device_us(
        lambda: gated_delta_rule_mtp(**rep, verify_parents=parent))
    return out

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"device {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)} {torch.cuda.get_device_capability()}")
    print("CUDA-event timed under graph replay, 50 iters. Star tree (parent[i]=0).\n")
    hdr = (f"{'B':>5} {'T':>3} {'HV':>3} {'HK':>3} | {'triton tree':>12} "
           f"{'FI prod chain':>14} {'FI RSSM chain':>14} {'FI RSSM tree':>13} | "
           f"{'triton/FItree':>14}")
    print(hdr); print("-" * len(hdr))
    for B, T, HV, HK in [(32, 8, 8, 2), (32, 8, 32, 8), (128, 8, 8, 2),
                         (512, 8, 8, 2), (512, 4, 8, 2), (128, 8, 32, 8)]:
        r = row(B, T, HV, HK)
        print(f"{B:>5} {T:>3} {HV:>3} {HK:>3} | {r['triton_tree']:12.1f} "
              f"{r['fi_chain_prod']:14.1f} {r['fi_replayssm_chain']:14.1f} "
              f"{r['fi_replayssm_tree']:13.1f} | "
              f"{r['triton_tree'] / r['fi_replayssm_tree']:13.2f}x")
```

</details>

Two test files, 31 passed together (229 with the spec-fold file) on a
B200 (SM100); the reference test also runs on CPU and so on every GitHub

`tests/gdn/test_verify_delta_rule_tree.py`: 19 tests, no SM gate.

- chain parents are bit-identical to `parents=None` (output, final
state, intermediate states), as a list and as an `int32 [B, T]` tensor
- six topologies (chain, fork at root, topk=4 depth 2, lopsided, star,
topk=2 depth 4) match an FP64 per-node ancestor-replay oracle to < 1e-5
relative, on outputs and on per-node states
- per-request topologies in one batch each match their own oracle
- a star tree agrees with the chain on token 0 and differs by > 1e-2
relative on every later token, so a reference that ignored `parents`
would fail
- malformed parents raise `ValueError`: forward reference, self-parent,
below -1, token 0 with a parent, wrong length, wrong batch

Existing callers of `verify_delta_rule` in
`tests/gdn/test_decode_delta_rule.py` re-run unchanged
(`test_verify_kernel_mtp`, the fp16 and dtype-interleaving cases, the
MTP output-buffer cases).

`tests/gdn/test_replayssm_tree_verify.py` checks the tree output against
an independent FP64 oracle that replays each node's own ancestor path
from the checkpoint, over six topologies (chain, fork-at-root, topk=4
depth 2, lopsided, star, topk=2 depth 4). Every topology lands at
1.82e-3 relative error, which is the kernel's own bf16-output/TF32-MMA
error and not an artifact of the mask — the chain computed *through* the
masked path agrees with the untouched chain path to four digits. Over
six topologies now that the list is shared. Two further tests guard the
ends: that omitting `verify_parents` is bit-identical across runs, and
that a forked tree diverges from the chain answer on every node whose
ancestor set differs while agreeing on node 0, which has none. A ninth
test runs the kernel in a child process with
`FLASHINFER_VALIDATE_VERIFY_PARENTS=1`: a valid tree exits cleanly and a
forward parent trips the device-side assert.
`tests/gdn/test_replayssm_spec_fold.py` is unchanged and still passes
(198 passed, 16 skipped) on SM100.

## Reviewer Notes

`verify_parents` is plumbed to the public `gated_delta_rule_mtp`
entrypoint; the only consumer is the fork SGLang PR above. SGLang calls
the same concept `retrieve_parent_token`; we are keeping
`verify_parents` for now and will raise the name with SGLang when the
integration goes upstream. The GDN cache key gains `HAS_PATHS`, so chain
callers never compile the tree variant, but a second pair of eyes on
that is welcome.

`verify_parents` requires `parent[i] < i`, because the kernel builds its
Gram matrix for `j < i` and the epilogue iterates increasing `i`. SGLang
satisfies this by construction, since the parent list is accumulated per
draft step and concatenated, giving a level-by-level layout. The kernel
does not check it by default: a host-side tensor comparison forces a
device-to-host sync, which in the GDN prototype cost 48 µs per call,
larger than the whole kernel at small batch. Setting
`FLASHINFER_VALIDATE_VERIFY_PARENTS=1` enables a `torch._assert_async`
check that fails closed on device without a sync, following the existing
`FLASHINFER_CAKE_GDN_VALIDATE_SLOTS` pattern. With the check off, an
entry outside `[0, i)` is treated as no parent, so a malformed array
gives a wrong answer for that token but never reads outside the kernel's
shared-memory tables.

On the GDN side `T ≤ 8` continues to apply, but that is the ReplaySSM
kernel's pre-existing cap from `s_decay`/`s_beta`/`s_rawk`, not
something the weight matrix introduces.

Trees are declined on `gdn_decode_bf16_state`, the register-resident
kernel SGLang launches for chains on SM100: a tree needs a distinct
state per node, which that kernel cannot represent. The SGLang
integration therefore runs tree verify through `cache_replayssm=True` on
this kernel and leaves the chain path where it is.

The vLLM drop-in entry point passes a dummy tensor for ABI parity and
does not support trees; vLLM has no tree speculative decode at all
today, so there is nothing to wire it to.

With a tree there is no single "final" state. `new_state` is the state
after token `T-1` along its own path (which is the chain's final state
when `parents` is the chain), and `intermediate_states[:, t]` is the
state after token `t` along its path. Committing an accepted path is the
caller's job and is out of scope here.

The oracle in the test replays each node's full ancestor path from the
initial state; the reference memoizes one state per node and continues
from the parent's. They share no code path, so agreement to 1e-5 is a
real cross-check rather than a tautology.

### [77bf17d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/77bf17dccc682b21c341cf0c75ec2857a993e52b)

- **作者**: Ka-Hyun Nam
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T20:59:04Z
- **提交信息**: feat(gdn): accept_paths for tree commits; tracked commits on the tcgen05 fold (#6257)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds an optional `accept_paths: int32 [B, T]` argument to
`gated_delta_rule_replayssm_commit`, so the ReplaySSM commit can fold a
root-to-node path through a draft tree instead of only a contiguous
prefix. This is the commit half of tree-structured speculative decoding
for GDN; #6155 is the verify half. The two are independent kernels and
merge in either order, but an engine needs both to run a tree.

Tree speculative decoding (EAGLE-2/3 with `topk > 1`) accepts a path
through the draft that in general is not a prefix: with three draft
tokens a request may accept `{0, 2}` and reject the sibling at row 1.
`accept_lens` is a count and cannot express that, and the commit kernel
replays rows `0..n-1` by loop counter, so the rejected row reaches the
checkpoint. That is measured, not inferred: poisoning row 1 with NaN and
asking for three accepted tokens NaNs 100% of the committed state on
`main`.

The recurrence is path-agnostic. Both folds build the Gram matrix and
the coefficient recurrence over staged positions, not cache rows, so an
ordered path keeps the strictly-triangular structure and only the load
index moves. The change is four load sites in the SIMT fold and three in
the tcgen05 fold. `accept_paths=None` compiles a `HAS_PATHS=False`
variant with no gather, which is bitwise identical to the kernel before
this PR, so chain decoding pays nothing. `accept_lens` is retained as
that chain fast path, and `row j` of request `i` is read only when `j <
accept_lens[i]`.

Out-of-range rows are clamped into `[0, T)` rather than rejected,
because checking values on the host would need a device synchronization.
`track_steps` needs no change: it already counts positions along the
accepted sequence, which is what a path replays. The fp64 reference in
`flashinfer/trace/templates/gdn.py` gains the same argument.

Second commit: explicit `backend="tcgen05"` accepts tracked commits.
Until now any commit with `track_state_indices` raised on tcgen05 and
fell back to the FP32 SIMT fold under `auto`. The SIMT fold gains a
`TRACK_ONLY` constexpr: a row with a live track slot and an in-range
step replays only up to that step and writes only the track slot, every
other CTA exits at the top. With tracking on tcgen05 the dispatcher runs
that pass first, against the untouched checkpoint, then the tcgen05 fold
commits the live slots as before; the ordering is what makes it correct.
Under this route the snapshot is FP32 while the live slot is TF32, so
the two copies of one logical state differ at TF32 level, about 1e-5
max-abs on B200.

`backend="auto"` keeps every tracked commit on SIMT. The snapshot pass
replays each live tracked row on top of the full fold, and its cost
grows with the fraction of rows whose track slot is live, which the host
cannot see. Measured on B200, all 36 layers in one launch, T=8, identity
paths, CUDA-graph timed with CUPTI, cold L2, median of 50, in
microseconds:

| B | HV | tracked rows live | SIMT (auto) | snapshot pass + tcgen05
fold (explicit) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13 | 32 | none | 471 | 462 |
| 13 | 32 | 1 in 8 | 483 | 538 |
| 13 | 32 | 1 in 4 | 495 | 620 |
| 64 | 8 | none | 669 | 578 |
| 64 | 8 | 1 in 8 | 680 | 667 |
| 64 | 8 | 1 in 4 | 692 | 761 |

The explicit route wins only when few or no tracked rows are live, so it
stays an opt-in for callers that know their live fraction; SGLang's
`extra_buffer` strategy, which passes track tensors on every commit,
continues to get SIMT by default.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Builds on #5314 and the merged #6229 and #6496. Commit-side companion to
#6155.

All in `tests/gdn/test_replayssm_spec_fold.py`, run on a B200 (SM100):

case. Verify a 4-token draft, NaN-poison rows 1 and 3, commit path `[0,

- `test_replayssm_commit_path_cycles`: every accepted length from 0 to T

- `test_replayssm_commit_identity_path_is_bitwise_identical`: the
no-gather fast path and an explicit identity path agree with zero

- `test_replayssm_commit_path_cuda_graph`: verify plus path commit

- `test_replayssm_commit_dispatch`: tracked commits select SIMT under

- The explicit tcgen05 plus tracking cases of

and null track slots against an fp64 reference, on both the identity and

Whole file on B200 with both commits on main: 279 passed, 15 skipped.

## Reviewer Notes

Nothing in SGLang or vLLM passes a path yet. The `[B, T]` padded layout
with `accept_lens` as the valid count was chosen to match how SGLang's
EAGLE verify already emits accepted positions, and the SGLang
integration that drives it is in progress on top of this PR and #6155.

Rows are documented as distinct within a request but not checked, for
the same device-sync reason as the range check. A repeated row replays
the same token twice, which is a semantic error on the caller's side
rather than a memory-safety one; every load stays within `[0, T)` after
the clamp.

The "bitwise identical" claim for `accept_paths=None` was checked
directly rather than by inspection: the four touched source files were
reverted to the parent commit in a scratch copy, `gated_delta_rule_mtp`
plus commit was run on both backends at T in {4, 6, 8} and B in {1, 5}
with mixed accept lengths, and all twelve committed checkpoints are
`torch.equal` to the ones produced by this branch. `HAS_PATHS` is part
of both compile-cache keys and of the on-disk kernel name, so a chain
caller never loads a tree variant.

For unaccepted staged positions the tcgen05 kernel fills `s_decay` and
`s_beta` from the clamped padding row rather than from the rejected row.
The only consumer of those positions is the coefficient loop, which is
guarded by `step < n_commit`, and the corresponding key rows are zero,
so the values are never used. The existing NaN-poison tests already
prove that on the chain path; the path tests poison row 0, which is the
padding row, and still pass.

On the second commit: the tracked snapshot pass reads the checkpoint, so
it must run before the fold; both launch on the caller's stream in that
order. Its full grid exits early on untracked rows, and each live
tracked row replays up to its tracked step on the SIMT fold, which is
why the route only pays off with few live tracks; a compacted grid over
tracked rows would need a device-to-host count or an indirect launch.
The fp64 reference clamps path rows the same way the kernels do. Most of
the commit-kernel diff is the SIMT launch moving into a nested helper so
it can be invoked twice with different constexprs; the kernel body
changes are the `TRACK_ONLY` gate on `is_live`, the loop bound, and the
final store.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Replay accepted sequences using explicitly selected cache rows instead
of only sequential rows. Without a specified path, replay remains
sequential; out-of-range rows are clamped.
* Tracked state snapshots stay aligned with accepted positions. On
supported hardware, automatic backend selection uses SIMT when tracking
is enabled, while explicit `tcgen05` supports sequence lengths of 4–8.
* **Documentation**
* Clarified replay-path behavior, row bounds, tracking, and backend
selection. The accepted-path input requirements are also documented.

### [4c323c1](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/4c323c122849d9603ece31e5210a5263fab696a7)

- **时间**: 2026-11-09T20:52:00Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_moe_grouped_gemm_nondet_train): queue-walk weight-gradient tiles on SM100 and SM103 (#9287)

`cake_moe_grouped_gemm_nondet_train` is the non-deterministic Cake BF16
MoE grouped GEMM for training. It covers the forward pass, the data
gradient and the weight gradient. The weight gradient writes BF16 or
FP32 output, or accumulates into `main_grad` (fused FP32 or composed
BF16 accumulation). On sm_100a and sm_103a, this PR changes some
weight-gradient stages with a 512-wide k-tile. Where it is faster, they
now claim output tiles dynamically in order (a queue walk) instead of
using a fixed strided walk. sm_107a routes are unchanged. Outputs still
repeat bit for bit from run to run. No measured shape is slower than
`main`. Against `main`, the counts of shapes that are faster (beyond the
A/A band on both GPUs) / within noise / slower are: B200 9 / 9 / 0,
GB200 4 / 11 / 0, GB300 11 / 6 / 0 and R200 0 / 6 / 0. The largest gains
are:
- B200 wgrad acc32 down E8 M131072 one-empty: 2.5644 → 2.4518 ms
(×1.046)
- GB300 wgrad acc32 down E16 M131072: 2.0107 → 1.9516 ms (×1.030)
- GB200 wgrad down E16 M131072: 2.3167 → 2.2650 ms (×1.023)

The deterministic counterpart is `cake_moe_grouped_gemm_det_train`, and
the family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

GPUs: B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs), GB300 (sm_103a)
and R200 / VR200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), with CUDA 13.4. Times are in
milliseconds of CUPTI GPU time with a cold L2. Each is the median of 16
interleaved rounds in one process per GPU, averaged over 2 GPUs per
shape. `main` is this kernel on main today. `det` is
`cake_moe_grouped_gemm_det_train` on main. `non-Cake` is the fastest
non-Cake grouped GEMM of the same precision for that shape, named in the
cell. The × columns are baseline / new, so a value above 1 means the new
code is faster. ▲ marks shapes faster than `main` beyond the A/A band on
both GPUs. The tables list the shapes whose routes this PR changes, plus
controls. All other representative shapes run the same programs as on

### [5e2ef46](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5e2ef46fdc2f9c3c3c549e8ce6c0aa22f852b7ec)

- **作者**: Jonas Li
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T20:33:18Z
- **提交信息**: fix(kda): fence Small-BH K1 gate-stage writes for the async proxy before their TMA store (#9229)

## 📌 Description

The Small-BH K1 gate warpgroup writes each Qd/Kd tile into a
shared-memory stage with ordinary stores and commits the stage; warp 0
of the MMA warpgroup then TMA-stores the tile to global memory. Nothing
made those stores visible to the async proxy first, so on a persistent
grid whose blocks process many tiles, the TMA store could read the stage
before the writes land and carry the values of the tile that last used
it — two tiles before — into the output.

This PR fences the shared-memory writes
(`fence.proxy.async.shared::cta`, `cute.arch.fence_view_async_shared()`)
in the gate warpgroup before it commits the stage, which is the order
the CUDA Programming Guide gives for a TMA store of shared memory
written by threads: the writing threads fence, then synchronize, then
one thread issues the store.

TensorRT-LLM vendors this kernel and hit the race through a scheduling
knob that shrinks the persistent grid (NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#21908, nvbugs
7049820): with three active clusters, 590 of 1000 launches wrote stale
Qd tiles, and every wrong value equaled the full-grid value of the tile
that last used that shared-memory stage. With the fence, 0 of 1000
launches differ (GB300, CuTe DSL 4.8.0), and full-grid K1 time is
unchanged (10.9 us before, 11.0 us after on the failing test's batch;
180.4 us before, 185.1 us after with three blocks).

A regression test compares 32 three-block K1 launches bitwise with a
reference launch that gives every scheduled tile its own block, so the
reference itself reuses no stage.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#21908 (TensorRT-LLM-side fix for the same race;
TRT-LLM vendors this kernel and carries an equivalent local patch)
- nvbugs 7049820

## 📌 Description

Restore runtime-length QToken sparse attention performance by
asynchronously caching bounded query-membership prefixes in shared
memory, with a global-memory fallback for longer routes. Enable the same
representation for eligible BF16 Keeps routes. Add opt-in
`run(validate=False)` after preparation to reduce repeated host
validation.

FP8 prefill, Hq/Hkv=12/1, D256, G4, Q=4096, context=32768, top-k=512,
block/page=4/32, no split-KV. Medians of 50 single-call CUDA graphs
after 10 warmups, with a random 256 MiB cache scrub per sample:

| GPU | Before (15482962a) | After | Gap vs pre-regression e46d85600 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B200 | 485.38 µs | 415.74 µs | +1.00% |
| B300 | 409.60 µs | 355.36 µs | +1.47% |
| Rubin ts1 (208 SMs) | 232.77 µs | 210.96 µs | +0.74% |

Both measurement orders meet the 2% historical gate. BF16 prefill and
FP8 bs64/sq4 decode (split and nonsplit) match or beat the historical
baseline on all three GPUs. Host enqueue with `validate=False` is about
15 µs on B300 and 10 µs on Rubin.

- **提交信息**: perf(trtllm-gen): require longer mainloops for multi-wave KV splits (#9261)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_GEN_MULTI_WAVE_KV_SPLIT=1` can increase KV splits for
a short sliding window even when the history is long, making decode
slower. Cap the opt-in increase so each raised split retains at least 24
modeled KV mainloop tiles, using the effective attention window and the
selected kernel's KV step. Accept a partially capped increase only when
modeled CTA-wave utilization improves over the stock split.

This also applies to mode 2's fallback to mode 1; mode 2's normal
wave-fill policy is unchanged. Update the existing end-to-end tests for
short-window parity, accepted and rejected caps, and long-loop
capacity/reselection paths.

B300 latency in **µs**, comparing upstream main `c7fe5fea1` with this
PR. Shape: batch 48, one query token, Hq/Hkv=32/4, D=64, page size 64,
HND, history 143360, BF16 output. BF16/BF16 uses plain BF16 Q/K/V; FP8
is E4M3. Median of 10 CUDA graph replays, each containing 128 calls with
timing events outside the graph.

| Q / KV | Attention | Main, flag off | Main, flag 1 | This PR, flag 1 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 / BF16 | SWA 2048 | 18.30 | 30.20 | 18.30 |

### [6583dff](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6583dff7d7a7760b99110353f788f34c414f7534)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T20:18:46Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion): two-shot shared programs at world sizes 4 and 8 (#9284)

When a batch runs the two-shot program below the deferred range with
top_k 4 and the rank has a shared-expert operand, the binding now runs a
two-shot shared program at world sizes 4 and 8, and in place of the
two-shot early program a two-shot early shared program at world size 4
(bf16 / fp16, o110 / o111). In each token step these programs prefetch
the shared-expert row into L2 before the route loop and read that row
through the read-only non-coherent path. World size 8 keeps the
two-shot early program for its early batches. Protocol, workspace,
summation order and outputs are unchanged; each new program uses the
same cross-rank exchange as the program it replaces, and the choice
reads only the token count, the world size, top_k and whether a shared
expert is given. Twelve kernel files are added and the loader lists
them. The CPU dispatch test checks the new tables and the program
choice at world sizes 4 and 8 with and without a shared expert at
top_k 4 and 8 on both sides of each two-shot class edge, with mixed
ranks, at small_token_max 16 and 64; the GPU test's program mirror
follows.

### [59c5bce](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/59c5bce74f13748239a567aebf609d81e858ded3)

- **作者**: Adrian
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T19:54:25Z
- **提交信息**: ci: bound AI scope evidence before requesting recommendations (#9024)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Large PRs can exceed the 300,000-character evidence cap before the first
model call because changed-file patches, repository inventories and
routing files were assembled without an initial budget. For the saved PR
#9006 snapshot, the old selector built 536,116 characters and rejected
the request before inference.

Budget complete evidence objects while constructing both requests.
Preserve changed-file metadata first, prioritize changed tests and
nearby inventory entries, reserve room for model-requested bodies, and
report omissions explicitly. CI and source bodies stay complete. Check
the serialized context after credential redaction and log stage/section
sizes without source contents or credentials. Known configuration files
remain requestable after eager-read omissions. Per-path omission
diagnostics have a separate cap to preserve the source reservation.
Incomplete PR descriptions, omitted changed-file metadata, or a mismatch
between the files response count and captured PR metadata cannot
authorize a full-suite run. Matching counts alone do not establish
snapshot identity.

Add a local replay tool using saved GitHub JSON, cached Git objects and
a fake model. The 300,000-character cap is unchanged. Saved-snapshot
comparisons:

| PR | Original first request | Revised first request | Revised second
request |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| #8993 | 344,884 (rejected) | 247,691 | 282,333 |
| #9006 | 536,116 (rejected) | 249,329 | 253,133 |

All changed-file metadata was retained in both replays (150 and 390
files respectively). The second-stage fake request inspected
`tests/infra/test_sharding/test_bot_run_workflow.py` for #8993 and
`tests/attention/test_alibi.py` for #9006. These are offline sizing
measurements; no model or GPU benchmark is involved.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Addresses the evidence-size rejection observed on #8993 and reproduced
on #9006. Companion internal ci-bot MR:
https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/flashinfer/ci-bot/-/merge_requests/32.

### [ad44800](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ad448009c5f57b14603674d872f0ba917975ea57)

- **作者**: Dimitrios Bariamis
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T18:50:59Z
- **提交信息**: feat(mla): Declare and test compact-query sparse TRTLLM-GEN dimensions (#6249)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

TRTLLM-GEN sparse MLA already handles a 64-wide non-RoPE query with
latent rank 512 and RoPE dimension 64, but this configuration is missing
from the declared dimension list and dedicated regression coverage.

Add the 64/64/128/512 dimension tuple to the shared MLA utilities,
preserve its re-export from the core module, clarify the API
documentation, and add reference-based sparse decode tests for BF16 and
FP8 query/KV-cache inputs with batch sizes 1 and 3. These tests exercise
the existing TRTLLM-GEN kernel path; no CUDA kernel changes are
required.

## 🔍 Related Issues

None.

was not run).

### Latest validation: BF16 and FP8 compact-query regression tests

**4 tests passed in 18.94 seconds** on a remote NVIDIA GB300 (SM103),
with Python 3.12.3 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, at commit
`e233db920711e607890b74cf9f1e529e23047076`.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/attention/test_trtllm_gen_mla.py::test_trtllm_batch_decode_mla_sparse_compact_query --full -vv
```

The four cases cover BF16 and FP8 (`torch.float8_e4m3fn`) query/KV-cache
inputs, each with batch sizes 1 and 3. They use the compact-query
dimension tuple, a query length of 1, top-k 2048, variable sequence
lengths, and the explicit `trtllm-gen` backend. The existing helper
compares results against a PyTorch reference and checks output shape and
NaNs using the existing dtype-specific tolerances. No cases were
skipped.

Ruff lint and formatting checks and `git diff --check` passed for the
latest test changes. A subsequent local `pre-commit run --all-files`
using pre-commit 4.7.0 passed at the same commit without changing any
tracked files. All applicable hooks passed, including clang-format,
mypy, Ruff lint/format, and the experimental test scope selftest; the
symlink hook had no files to check.

### Earlier validation: broader MLA selection

Before the FP8 compact-query parametrization was added, **42 selected
tests passed** on NVIDIA B200 (SM100), Python 3.12.3, and PyTorch

pre-commit run --files flashinfer/mla/_core.py flashinfer/mla/_utils.py tests/attention/test_trtllm_gen_mla.py

### [848aa30](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/848aa30500c5ab781a6600c988011e0fcdfbcc1d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T18:47:36Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_det_train): column-task backward programs at small token counts and new small-T forward programs (#9277)

The Cake deterministic RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_det_train`) has 16 variants: a BF16 or an FP32
weight on H 256, 512, 1536, 2048, 4096, 5120 and 6144, plus the fused
residual add on H 6144 with either weight. Each variant has a forward
and a backward and a row-stride argument (contiguous rows, strided rows,
q / k head views), on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR changes, on
at least one of these architectures, the backward of 14 variants and the
forward of 12 variants. In the backward, it delivers column-task
programs at small token counts: one CTA sums each column of dw over
every row in a fixed order, so dw does not depend on the SM count. These
are one-row programs at T = 1 for H 512, 1536 and 2048 on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a, and small-T windows for the H 256 views, H 1536,
2048, 5120 and 6144 (sm_100a), H 4096, 5120 and 6144 (sm_103a) and H
512, 5120 and 6144 (sm_107a), each with its FP32-weight twin. In the
forward, it delivers programs that form rstd with the approximate
reciprocal square root at the smallest token counts of H 256, 512, 1536,
2048 and 5120 and of the residual H 6144 route on sm_100a and sm_103a.
The windows differ per architecture, and FP32-weight twins cover the
same windows. On sm_100a, it also delivers another residual H 6144
forward program above 4096 rows. The sm_107a forward is unchanged. The
baseline is the current FlashInfer main version of the same kernel.
Speedup is main / PR latency, so above 1 means the PR is faster. The
largest speedups over the 143 shape rows are all at T = 1. Backward:
2.346x on B200 (H 256 FP32-weight k view, 5.86 -> 2.50 us), 2.400x on
GB300 (H 512 row stride 576, 4.22 -> 1.76 us) and 2.059x on VR200 (H
2048, 3.36 -> 1.63 us). Training step: 1.617x on B200 (H 256 FP32-weight
k view, 10.14 -> 6.27 us), 1.525x on GB300 (H 2048, 7.71 -> 5.06 us) and
1.376x on VR200 (H 512 row stride 576, 6.56 -> 4.77 us). Forward: 1.353x
on B200 (H 256 FP32-weight k view, 2.21 -> 1.63 us) and 1.246x on GB300
(H 5120 FP32 weight, 2.59 -> 2.08 us); the VR200 forward is unchanged.
The PR changes the program of 38 of the 143 shape rows on B200, 48 on
GB300 and 22 on VR200, in at least one op. Across the 143 rows and four
ops, no cell is slower than main beyond the measured run-to-run noise on
any board. Rows whose programs do not change read between 0.97 and 1.03,
which is noise.

The non-deterministic version of this kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_nondet_train`) and the SiLU-gated RMSNorm
training kernels (`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`,
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_nondet_train`) are not changed here;
the family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

Measured on NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152
SMs) and dlcluster VR200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs; its driver reports the name
"NVIDIA Graphics Device"), with PyTorch 2.14.1 on CUDA 13.0 and nvcc
13.4.92 (CUDA 13.4). Each latency is the median CUPTI time of one
CUDA-graph replay with L2 flushed before each replay. Each table keeps
all 143 shape rows.

SMs); GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs); dlcluster VR200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs). CUDA

Shapes (BF16 input; BF16 weight unless noted; contiguous rows unless
noted; T = tokens): a = H 512, row stride 576; b = H 1536; c = H 2048; d

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* Added deterministic BF16 RMSNorm training support across additional
GPU architectures and tensor sizes, including forward normalization and
backward gradient calculations.
* Expanded available kernel variants and tuned execution paths for
different row counts and hidden sizes.
* **Bug Fixes**
* Updated backward routing and FP32/BF16 route matching to select
compatible kernel variants across more workloads.
* **Tests**
* Expanded coverage for additional row counts, architecture-specific
routing windows, and column-task execution paths.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [11c098f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/11c098fa319b7fa9f305720b0017c2e5f1958855)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T18:45:57Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_det_train): faster budget forms, log-prob calls and sm_107a GEMMs (#9272)

`flashinfer.cake_lm_head_det_train` is the deterministic chunked LM-head
training backend. It takes BF16 inputs, accumulates in FP32, and
produces outputs and gradients that are bitwise reproducible from run to
run. It has two entries:

- The loss entry, `cake_lm_head_det_train_loss`, with CE and policy
objectives.
- The log-probability entry, `cake_lm_head_det_train_logprob`, with an
optional scalar or per-token temperature.

The memory forms are sized against B. B is the memory an implementation
needs if it keeps the BF16 logits of the valid rows: `B = 2*T_v*V +
2*V*H + 2*T*H` bytes.

- T is the number of rows.
- T_v is the number of valid rows, meaning rows whose label is not -100.
- H is the hidden size.
- V is the vocabulary size.

The module has four memory forms:

- `memory_mode=None` (default) is the automatic form. For each call, it
picks the fast or the budget form against B, with a 2 % margin.
- `memory_mode="fast"` is the fast form. It keeps one chunk of logits
plus an FP32 `[V, H]` weight-gradient accumulator.
- `memory_mode="budget"` is the budget form. It limits the step peak.
- `memory_mode="keep_logits"` is the keep-logits form.

This PR follows #9211 and makes five changes. Every output and gradient
keeps the bits of `memory_mode="fast"`.

**1. New budget form `"partial_ip"` for calls with two or more chunks.**
It serves the loss and log-probability entries.

- It uses the split FP32 weight-gradient accumulator of `"fused_ip"`
(#9211), but only for the vocabulary rows [0, dw_rows). The two parts
are [0, a) and [a, dw_rows).
- The backward keeps the BF16 dz of the deferred last chunk.
- The backward casts the rows [0, dw_rows) in place, as `"fused_ip"`
does.
- It recomputes the other rows and reads the last chunk's block from the
kept dz. As a result, each block runs one logits GEMM fewer than in the
budget form `"partial"`.
- The automatic form now picks it wherever it picked `"partial"`:
- the two-chunk T 8117 rows (CE, policy, and log-prob with every
temperature);
- the #7545-shape rows with 33 % ignored (T 16384, H 6144, CE and
log-prob).

**2. Split accumulator in the log-probability budget backward.** The
log-probability entry's budget backward now runs the split accumulator
of `"fused_ip"`. These rows move from `"unfused"` to `"fused_ip"`:

- the four-chunk log-prob rows (T 16172 / 16231 / 16384, 5 % ignored,
every temperature);
- the H 5120 / V 248320, T 16384 log-prob rows.

**3. Kept one-chunk logits for the default log-probability call.**

- It applies to a default call. That is a call with no temperature and
no num_valid_rows, where a backward can follow, and that does not run
under `torch.utils.checkpoint`.
- The call's valid rows must fit one chunk.
- The call's fast backward must run no zero-gradient row skip. That
means the call has fewer valid rows than the device's skip floor: 1946
on sm_100a, 3891 on sm_103a and 4097 on sm_107a.
- Such a call keeps its BF16 logits (at most one chunk) from forward to
backward.
- The backward forms dz from these logits. It runs three GEMMs instead
of four.
- `memory_mode="fast"` or `set_logprob_one_chunk_keep(False)` turns it
off.
- In the tables, the following rows take it:
  - the T 2048 log-prob row with no temperature on GB300;
  - the T 2048 and T 4097 log-prob rows with no temperature on R200.
- On B200, these rows (5 % ignored) are at the floor and keep the
default form.

**4. One forward in the checkpointed step of opt-in log-probability
calls.**

- Opt-in log-probability calls pass num_valid_rows or
`memory_mode="budget"`, with or without temperature.
- These calls now hand their forward to the replay of a non-reentrant
checkpoint, as the default entry does. The checkpointed step therefore
runs one forward.
- `memory_mode="keep_logits"` now takes num_valid_rows.

**5. sm_107a GEMM rule tables.**

- On sm_107a, the GEMM rule tables now take the sm_103a entries.
- The exceptions are the logits rasters, the long-chunk dX ring and the
whole-chunk dX split.
- The whole-chunk dX split follows sm_100a.

**Measurement.** All numbers come from a same-GPU A/B of FlashInfer main
(c7fe5fea) against this PR (head 083bdf3c) merged onto that main.

- For each (row, temperature) pair, at least two units run on two
different GPUs. Each unit runs main, the PR and a second copy of the PR
in forward order, then in reverse order, with one process per tree.
- On R200, the T 2048 and T 4097 log-prob rows with no temperature were
measured again with four more units. The tables show that run.
- On GB300, the opt-in table pools four units per row, from two nodes.
- Times are CUPTI kernel times with the L2 cache flushed. Each process
runs 4 rounds x 4 iterations, and the result is the median per tree.
- Speedup is main / PR. Its 95 % CI comes from a hierarchical bootstrap
with 4000 resamples. The A/A band is max(1 %, the CI bound of PR-copy /
PR).
- GPUs: B200 (sm_100a, driver 580.82.07, 1000 W), GB300 (sm_103a, driver
580.159.03, 1400 W) and R200 (sm_107a, VR200 nodes with 212 SMs, driver

What the table shows:

- **num_valid_rows given.**
  - ckpt main/PR is 1.187-1.282 on GB300 and 1.194-1.310 on R200.
- On B200, ckpt main/PR is 0.993-1.057. There, main's checkpointed step
of the one-chunk rows already runs close to the plain step. The T 8117
rows reach 1.052-1.057.
  - Step main/PR is 1.044-1.077 for the T 8117 rows on every GPU.
- Other step cells are at parity. The exceptions are T 2048 with 33 %
ignored (B200 1.251, R200 1.041) and R200 T 4097 with no temperature
(1.011).
- **`memory_mode="budget"`.**
- ckpt main/PR is 1.171-1.267 on B200, 1.167-1.262 on GB300 and
1.168-1.294 on R200.
- Step is at parity. The exceptions are T 8117, at 1.050 / 1.053 / 1.076
(B200 / GB300 / R200), and R200 T 4097 with per-token temperature
(1.015).
- **`memory_mode="keep_logits"` with num_valid_rows.** Main runs this
form without num_valid_rows.
  - Step and ckpt main/PR are 0.991-1.034.
  - On GB300 and R200, step is 1.008-1.034.
- No cell of these call forms is slower beyond the band.

Across all five operations of these three call forms (90 cells per GPU),
the faster / parity / slower counts are:

- B200 (90 cells): 18 / 72 / 0
- GB300 (90 cells): 30 / 60 / 0
- R200 (90 cells): 45 / 45 / 0

### [7674754](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/76747542f738a2ad8fce14559c674e670184039d)

- **作者**: Akaash Parthasarathy
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T18:42:11Z
- **提交信息**: feat(moe_ep): autotune complete Mega and split EP plans (#8576)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Add `AutoConfig` to `MoEEpLayer` for selection between explicit Mega and
split configurations. Each split candidate pins its communication
backend; `candidate=i` forces one entry while retaining its inner
tuning.

Mega candidates reuse Rubin's variant and knob selection. Split
candidates enumerate eligible MoELayer backends and tactics and measure
each through the complete EP forward, including input preparation,
dispatch, compute, combine and output handling. The outer comparison
uses the same boundary. The existing MoELayer compute-only selection
path is unchanged.

The selected candidate and fixed configuration are stored in the managed
v2 cache. Prepared workspaces share transformed weights and retain
execution storage used by older captures. A separate commit skips
zero-row MXFP8 quantization launches so empty ranks can participate in
split execution.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to #7911.

### [7a88993](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7a88993d3a3365966929a235de1b8674190770c6)

- **作者**: Jimmy Zhou
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T17:47:02Z
- **提交信息**: test(batch_invariant): retry the profiled launch when the trace drops its kernel record (#9030)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`test_persistent_grid_is_the_device_co_resident_cluster_count` reads the
launched grid of a batch-invariant GEMM from a `torch.profiler` trace.
In the v0.7.4rc1 CI run it failed once on B200 / CUDA 12.9 with `no
kernel in the trace`: the profiler session around that single launch
held no kernel record, although the per-process probe just before it did
record kernels.

This is a test fragility, not a library bug:
- The same image and driver passed the same 52-test file in a later CI
run, and it passes locally on B200 with the CUDA 12.9 image (the full
file, plus 68 single-test runs from a cold JIT cache, some of them
concurrent and under CPU load). The failure did not reproduce.
- The kernel launch shows up as `cudaLaunchKernelExC` with a kernel
record of grid `[1, 1, 148]` whenever the trace is complete.

The fix profiles up to three launches. It zeroes the output before each
one, so the existing bitwise check now proves that each profiled launch
actually ran. The previous check could pass on the output of the
earlier, unprofiled call. A trace that never holds the kernel still
fails, so a real missing launch is not hidden.

Test-only change; no library code is touched.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Fixes #8967

## 📌 Description

Retry sccache release downloads to avoid failing JIT cache provider
builds on transient network errors, such as curl: (7) Connection
refused.
Both the archive and SHA-256 checksum downloads independently use the
same retry policy as Docker image pulls: four total attempts, with
5/10/20-second backoff. Builds still fail if all attempts are exhausted.
Checksum verification remains unchanged.

### [7319398](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7319398a36b6a1486b6004ac0af987dcd9366c17)

- **提交信息**: fix(cake_kimi_k3_latent_moe): cluster-scope cross-CTA landing barriers; GB300 ring-rows tail and full-tile front routes (#9275)

`flashinfer.experimental.kimi_k3_latent_moe` has four BF16 variants for
`sm_100a` and `sm_103a`: the Kimi-K3 Stable LatentMoE front and tail
projections of one rank, each for TP1 and TP8. This PR re-generates the
36 Cake programs whose two cluster CTAs exchange data: the 2-CTA front
and tail decode programs (up to 128 tokens) and three persistent tail
GEMM programs. Every barrier that receives a write from the other CTA
now works at cluster scope instead of CTA scope. Outputs stay bitwise
identical to FlashInfer main on every tested input on all four GPUs. On
GB300 only, nine shapes take new instances: a resident-B TP1 decode tail
(1-2 tokens with 7-16 routed partials, 3 tokens with 6-7) and a
full-tile split-finalize TP8 front at 128 tokens. Against the Cake
programs on FlashInfer main as of #9176, the geometric-mean speedup is
0.9996x on B200, 1.0002x on B300, 0.9998x on GB200 and 0.9999x on the
126 unchanged GB300 shapes. The nine re-routed GB300 shapes reach 1.069x
to 1.093x (TP1 tail) and 1.039x (TP8 front).

Cake also ships a TP12 fused tail of this block in `kimi_k3_tp12_tail`;
both packages are BF16 only and target `sm_100a` and `sm_103a`.

### [6d5f5be](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6d5f5be973f0e14e86cc706227bd5c8c9cb986f2)

- **作者**: Jimmy Zhou
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T17:39:04Z
- **提交信息**: fix(moe): accept strided partitioned C views in the Prims-TS BF16 launch IO (#9036)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

**Problem.** On SM107, every BF16 case of
`tests/prims_ts/test_moe_partition_execution.py` fails with `ValueError:
gemm1_output must be contiguous` (8 nodes in the v0.7.4rc1 CI run). The
partitioned BF16 Prims-TS MoE path cannot run at all.

**Cause.** The two-way `tp_n_tp_n` partition (#6832) has each FC1 shard
write a column slice of the shared intermediate buffer (`gemm1_output[:,
start:stop]`) and each FC2 shard write a column slice of `gemm2_output`,
passing the full row pitch as `c_row_stride`. These slices are
intentionally non-contiguous. The NVFP4, MXFP4 and FP8 launch-IO
builders already skip the contiguity check for the output buffer when
`c_row_stride` is set; `_validate_c_output_layout` checks its real
stride instead. #6608 later folded `gemm1_output`/`gemm2_output` into
the BF16 builder's contiguity loop without that exemption, so the BF16
builder now rejects the slices the partitioned runner passes. The two
PRs do not conflict textually.

**Fix.** In `build_bf16_launch_io`, skip the contiguity check for the
output buffer when `c_row_stride` is set, matching the other builders.
Everything else #6608 added is unchanged: `hidden_states`, both weights,
the activation input and the unpartitioned output buffer must still be
contiguous, and `_validate_c_output_layout` still rejects a strided
output whose row stride does not equal `c_row_stride`.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Fixes #9025

### [f5c6aa7](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f5c6aa76b9bc0997c4f727f91a4c5f3af2d5fc18)

- **作者**: Vincent
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T17:36:31Z
- **提交信息**: fix(gemm): key cuBLASLt tactics on algorithm descriptors, not heuristic indices (#6148)

## 📌 Description

The cuBLAS FP8 (`bmm_fp8(backend="cublas")`) and cuBLASLt BF16
(`mm_bf16(backend="cublaslt")` and the cuBLASLt candidate of
`backend="auto"`) runners used a position in
`cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic`'s list as the autotuner tactic. That
list is ranked for one exact problem, so it changes with M, while the
autotuner stores one tactic per M bucket.

Two consequences:

1. **BF16 runner: tuned entries never matched.**
`CublasltBf16GemmRunner.get_cache_key_extras` returned the exact `(M, N,
K, ...)`. Winners are stored with the bucket's synthesized M, lookups
use the caller's M, so outside a bucket boundary every lookup missed.
Under `autotune(True)` every call re-profiled the cuBLASLt tactics;
inside CUDA graph capture it raised `AutoTuner profiling cannot begin
during an active outer CUDA Graph capture`; outside tuning mode the
tuned tactic was silently not used.
2. **FP8 runner (and BF16 once keyed per bucket): index replay.** The
tuned index was replayed against the list enumerated at the actual M. On
an SM107 GPU (Rubin), comparing the list at the bucket M with the list
at another M of the same bucket, e.g. N=4096, K=7168: bucket 512 vs
M=300 -> 7/7 FP8 and 8/8 BF16 positions name a different algorithm, and
none of the bucket's algorithms appear in the M=300 list at all; bucket
768 vs M=513 is the same. So an in-range index ran an algorithm that was
never profiled.

This PR makes the tactic the algorithm itself:

- **Tactic = descriptor.** A cuBLASLt tactic is the 64-byte
`cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` as a tuple of eight uint64 words. It is hashable
and round-trips through `autotune(cache=...)` JSON and the `autotune_v2`
managed store unchanged. `-1` is still the heuristic default.
- **Candidates at the bucket's M.** `get_valid_tactics` enumerates at
`AutoTuner.get_effective_map_to_tuning_buckets(config)(M)` (same mapper
source as the cuDNN override-shape runners, so
`autotune(tuning_buckets=..., round_up=...)` overrides apply). The BF16
extras drop M, N and K (N and K are already in the autotuner's input
shapes; M is bucketed there) and keep compute dtype and bias alignment;
the FP8 extras were already dtype-only.
- **Validated at run time.** New `mm_bf16_cublaslt_run_with_descriptor`
/ `bmm_fp8_run_with_descriptor` entry points replace the index-based
`*_run_with_algo`. They check the descriptor for the actual problem with
`cublasLtMatmulAlgoCheck`, including its workspace requirement against
the provided workspace. If cuBLASLt rejects it (another M of the bucket,
a stale descriptor persisted by a different cuBLASLt, a corrupted
value), the heuristic's top algorithm for the actual problem runs
instead. The outcome is memoized in C++ per (descriptor, exact problem,
device, workspace size), so the steady state is a hash lookup with no
host work that would break graph capture. During profiling, a descriptor
that does not apply raises, so the autotuner disqualifies it instead of
timing the fallback.
- **Legacy integer tactics** fail the runners' `validate_tactic` hook,
so a cached index from an older cache is treated as a miss rather than
being misread.
- **Version handling:** both the v1 cache metadata (`_collect_metadata`)
and the v2 environment hash already include `cublas_version`, so a cache
written under another cuBLAS/cuBLASLt is not loaded; the AlgoCheck
fallback covers anything that slips through. The docstring now says this
field also covers the descriptors.

`tactic=-1` behaviour and the public APIs are unchanged.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Closes #6145

## Reviewer Notes

- The FP8 `tactic=-1` path still calls `bmm_fp8` (heuristic per call),
as before. The BF16 `-1` path now resolves the heuristic default in C++
(memoized) instead of a Python per-exact-M list cache.
- Candidates are enumerated with the synthesized profile tensors at the
bucket's M. Example: tuning at M=600 profiles a "600" bucket whose key
maps to 768, and the candidates come from M=768. A candidate that
AlgoCheck rejects at the synthesized M is disqualified during profiling.
- The C++ memo grows by one small entry per distinct (descriptor, exact
M, ...) seen, like the per-shape list cache it replaces.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* cuBLASLt FP8 and BF16 tuning now uses reusable algorithm descriptors
that can be resolved for different matrix sizes and runtime conditions.
* Algorithm enumeration can target a specified matrix size, and tuned
tactics use descriptors instead of numeric algorithm indices.
* Calls report whether a supplied descriptor was used; missing or
unsuitable descriptors fall back to the default heuristic algorithm.
* **Bug Fixes**
* BF16 matrix multiplication continues to produce results when algorithm
enumeration returns no candidates.

### [057966f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/057966f9e864f6944f38ec6f182afea6f0046936)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T17:25:38Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_nondet_train): faster backward windows on SM100, SM103 and SM107 (#9273)

Cake's RMSNorm training kernel comes in these variants: three input
forms (2-D rows, strided rows, and per-head 3-D q and k), BF16
activations with a BF16 or FP32 weight (`f32` in the shape column), and
a plain form and a residual-add fused form. Each has a forward and a
backward pass. This PR moves four backward windows of the
nondeterministic version (`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_nondet_train`) to
faster programs. Forward routes and all other backward routes are
unchanged. The baseline is the same kernel on FlashInfer main.

The changed windows and their speedups against main (x main = main / PR)
are listed below for bwd, fwdbwd (forward plus backward) and step
(training step). Each range covers every measured T in the window and
every A/B run, including T values that fall between the table's shapes:
- GB300 (sm_103a), H4096 bf16, T in (10239, 32768]: the pair-row single
kernel, which main already runs above T 32768. 19 measured T from 10240
to 32768: bwd 1.038-1.063x, fwdbwd 1.016-1.042x, step 1.013-1.028x.
- GB300 (sm_103a), H6144 bf16, T in (24575, 32768]: the pair-row single
kernel, which main already runs above T 32768. T 24576, 28672 and 32768:
bwd 1.020-1.028x, fwdbwd 1.010-1.016x, step 1.007-1.011x.
- B200 (sm_100a), H256 with an FP32 weight, rows in (524288, 864240],
i.e. q[T,24,256] strided f32 at T in (21845, 36010]: the deterministic
pair, which main runs up to 524288 rows. 5 T from 21846 to 36010: bwd
1.108-1.122x, fwdbwd 1.068-1.076x, step 1.049-1.056x.
- VR200 (sm_107a), H2048 bf16, T in (50688, 65536]: a new compensated
deterministic pair. 5 T from 50689 to 65536: bwd 1.167-1.207x, fwdbwd
1.085-1.104x, step 1.062-1.077x.

Each table below has the same 143 rows (shape, T). The rows inside these
windows have no mark on x main: 1 on B200 (q[T,24,256] strided f32 at T
32768), 13 on GB300 (H4096 bf16 at T 14928 to 32768, and H6144 bf16 at T
32768) and 1 on VR200 (H2048 bf16 at T 65536). Every other row runs the
same programs as main and is marked (s) or (s*).

Across fwd, bwd, fwdbwd and step (572 cells per GPU), this PR is faster
/ at parity / slower than main in 48 / 521 / 3 cells on B200, 87 / 478 /
7 on GB300 and 49 / 517 / 6 on VR200. Every cell whose program changed
is faster than main: 3 on B200, 39 on GB300 and 3 on VR200. Every slower
cell runs the same programs as main in both trees (marked (s*)) and was
slower in both A/B runs. These cells show measurement spread on
unchanged programs. Over all same-program cells of the first A/B run,
including the extra window rows, the faster and slower calls are
balanced: 40 / 38 of 582 on B200, 47 / 51 of 533 on GB300 and 44 / 37 of
573 on VR200.

Against the deterministic Cake kernel (x det = det / PR'), this PR's
kernel is faster / at parity / slower across all four ops in 114 / 333 /
124 (+1 N/A) cells on B200, 82 / 412 / 78 on GB300 and 84 / 475 / 13 on
VR200. In the backward tables the counts are 41 / 59 / 43, 29 / 89 / 25
and 28 / 111 / 4. Rows whose PR' value is marked (f) were measured on
this PR's final base, FlashInfer main with the deterministic package of
#9217:
- B200 (21 rows): H2048 bf16 at T 1024 to 16384, H4096 bf16 at T 4096 to
16384, H6144 bf16 at T 1024 and 4096, and q[T,24,256] strided f32 at T
32768
- GB300 (19 rows): H2048 bf16 at T 4096 to 16384, H4096 bf16 at T 4096
to 16384, and H6144 bf16 at T 1024 and 4096

#9217 made the deterministic backward faster on those rows. There, the
deterministic kernel is now faster than this PR's kernel in bwd, fwdbwd
and step (det / PR' 0.81-0.99 on B200, 0.82-0.99 on GB300), and the

Timing: median CUPTI span of one CUDA-graph replay after an L2 flush
(persisting L2 reset). main and PR come from the A/B run: 4 GPU
processes, 201 replays each in 3 interleaved rounds, pooled; A B B A,
each value the mean of the tree's two runs; x main = main / PR. det, PR'
and the non-Cake arm come from one shared run (x det = det / PR', x SOTA
= non-Cake / PR'). Non-Cake = the fastest arm of the same precision
class (BF16 x/y/dx, FP32 dw); d / nd = its measured run-to-run bitwise
class. Marks on x main: (s) same program: both trees launch the same
programs with the same launch records for this cell; (s*) same program,
slower than main in both A/B runs; (r) the first A/B run called this
cell slower, the rerun did not (the rerun's call counts). Source of det
/ PR' / non-Cake (mark on PR'): no mark = measured with this PR's kernel
package (base FlashInfer main bc47d043; harness v8.5.1: two runs on
different GPUs, pooled; latency = mean of the CUDA-graph instance
medians); (f) = measured on this PR's final tree (base FlashInfer main
bb5cc673 with the deterministic package of FlashInfer #9217), same
harness; (p1) = the previous PR's record (harness v8.4: median of the
pooled replays): this PR launches the same programs for that cell and
the deterministic program is unchanged. † on the non-Cake arm: timed in
fewer GPU processes than PR' (previous record).

Arms: `compile` = torch.compile (mode max-autotune-no-cudagraphs);
`compile_def` = torch.compile (default mode); `compile_def_detalg` =
torch.compile (default mode) compiled under
torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True); `compile_detalg` =
torch.compile (max-autotune-no-cudagraphs) compiled under
torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True); `cudnn_fe` = cuDNN frontend
1.32.2 RMSNorm (norm_fprop / norm_bprop); `fla` = fla-core 0.6.0
(flash-linear-attention) rms_norm; `liger_cutedsl` = Liger-Kernel 0.8.5
RMSNorm, CuTe-DSL backend; `quack` = QuACK 0.6.5 RMSNorm (FP32 dw from
FP32 per-SM partials); `quack_tuned` = QuACK 0.6.5 RMSNorm, autotuned.

Cake also ships a deterministic version of this kernel,
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_det_train` (the det column above), and a
SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel in both versions
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`,
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_nondet_train`); all ship on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a.

The full per-op tables for all three GPUs (fwd, bwd, fwdbwd and step)
follow in PR comments: the A/B comparison against main with A/A bands,
and the det / fastest non-Cake / PR comparison.
