### [d9a96ac](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d9a96ac933090f4107df6f7ca864b1fb64dc7b2b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T11:57:11Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_causal_conv1d_det_kcp): single-rank forward program as the KCP forward's main launch (#9225)

The Cake packed width-4 depthwise causal conv1d + SiLU training kernel
(BF16 activations, FP32 accumulation) has four forms: deterministic and
non-deterministic, each single-rank and context-parallel (KCP). The
single-rank forms also take BF16 taps and an optional bias. The KCP
forms take FP32 taps and no bias. This PR updates the forward of the
deterministic KCP form (`flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_det_train_kcp`:
`cake_causal_conv1d_det_kcp` / `cake_causal_conv1d_det_kcp_multi`),
which both backward routes share; every backward launch is unchanged.
The KCP forward now runs as two launches: a main launch runs the
single-rank forward's program on the rank's fragments and reads no
exchanged history row, then after the forward halo exchange a small new
program rewrites `y` of the first rows of each fragment that has
history, so `y` stays bitwise equal to the previous one-launch forward.
On sm_107a the multi entry launches its first tensor's main program
while the halo exchange is in flight, and its other tensors' main
launches follow the exchange; elsewhere, and for the single-tensor entry
everywhere, the main launch follows the exchange. The baseline is the
previous Cake version: the same package on FlashInfer main (3b389a974,
which includes #9190), run back to back on the same GPU. The later
change to this package on main (#9240) touches only single-rank backward
routes, which the KCP form does not launch.

Default route (`cooperative=False`), B200 / GB300 / VR200:
- fwd: 1.074x-1.194x / 1.032x-1.112x / 1.026x-1.155x
- fwd+bwd: 1.031x-1.075x / 1.015x-1.037x / 1.014x-1.056x
- checkpointed step: 1.042x-1.105x / 1.020x-1.054x / 1.017x-1.076x
- bwd: 0.989x-1.004x / 0.996x-1.004x / 0.993x-1.006x; slower beyond the
A/A band: B200 6 of 15, up to 1.1% (2.1 us); GB300 1 of 9, 0.3% (1.3
us); VR200 1 of 9, 0.7% (1.7 us)

`cooperative=True` (its backward launch is the same as on main; its
fwd+bwd and checkpointed-step rows include the changed forward), B200 /
GB300 / VR200:
- fwd+bwd: 1.025x-1.069x / 1.011x-1.038x / 1.012x-1.049x
- checkpointed step: 1.037x-1.101x / 1.017x-1.056x / 1.014x-1.066x
- bwd: 0.995x-1.003x / 0.997x-1.004x / 0.995x-1.006x; slower beyond the
A/A band: B200 1 of 15, 0.5% (3.4 us); GB300 2 of 9, up to 0.3% (1.8 us)

Every bwd row (both routes) launches the same programs as on main, so
those rows measure run-to-run variation.

| GPU | shape | phase | main (us) | this PR (us) | speedup | A/A band |

*Table 1. Default route (`cooperative=False`), 15 shapes on B200 and 9
on GB300 and VR200: three single-rank and six CP4 shapes per GPU, plus
six CP8 shapes on the 8-GPU B200 node. The table names each shape. Times
are in microseconds, each the slowest rank. They are measured with CUDA
events around the phase, cold L2, and host enqueue hidden behind a short
spin on the stream ("ahead" timing). Each run is the median of 12
interleaved rounds. Runs go main, this PR, this PR, main on the same
GPU(s). Main is the mean of runs 1 and 4; this PR is the mean of runs 2
and 3. Speedup = main / this PR (above 1: this PR faster). A/A band =
max(|run1 - run4| / main, |run2 - run3| / this PR). A row counts as
faster or slower only when its speedup differs from 1 by more than the
band. Slower-than-band counts and sizes in the summary use the unrounded
measurements, so a row printed as 1.000x can count as slower. In "up to
X% (Y us)", the largest relative and the largest absolute slowdown can
come from different shapes. Checkpointed step = 2 fwd + bwd. CPn =
context parallel over n ranks. PyTorch 2.14.1 (CUDA 13.0 runtime);

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added an alternative two-launch forward path for deterministic causal
convolution. It can overlap computation with history exchange, then
update outputs that depend on received history.
* The forward path is selected according to supported GPU architecture
and launch settings, and is available for single- and multi-tensor
calls.
  * Added prebuilt kernel support for select newer GPU architectures.
* **Bug Fixes**
* The two-launch path produces outputs and history matching the existing
one-launch path.

### [2024da3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2024da3b94b0531775b282f58578640c2ca5b15c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T11:55:13Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det): faster backward for value-head groups of three (HV = 3H) (#9238)

`flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train` is the deterministic (bitwise run-to-run
repeatable) chunked gated delta rule training kernel. It runs forward
and backward over variable-length documents and supports activation
checkpointing and value-head groups (HV a multiple of H). It has
variants along three axes: BF16 q/k/v with FP32 or BF16 beta, q/k L2
norm fused into the kernel or done by the caller, and q/k/v as head
views of one packed projection row or as separate contiguous tensors.
This PR delivers the backward for value-head groups of three (HV = 3H),
with FP32 and BF16 beta, on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. It sums the
FP32 dq and dk partials of the group's three value heads before a single
rounding to BF16. The adjoint state scan adds the FP32 dv_local term to
dv before its one rounding. When q, k and v are head views of one packed
projection row, the backward writes dq, dk and dv straight into one
packed gradient row. The forward is unchanged, so o and the final state
keep their bits. The gradients get new bits and are still bitwise
repeatable run to run. Compared with main, no row is slower on B200,
GB300 or R200. Backward is up to 1.10x faster on B200, 1.12x on GB300
and 1.11x on R200 (1.10x on B200 and GB300 and 1.11x on R200 for H/HV
2/6 with 259,174 tokens in 2 sequences, gB). fwd+bwd is up to 1.06x,
1.07x and 1.08x faster, and ckpt up to 1.05x, 1.04x and 1.07x. Forward
stays at about 1.00x. The comparison with the fastest non-Cake
implementation takes the best per row of cuDNN frontend 1.32.2, FLA
0.6.0 and FlashQLA 0.1.3. FlashQLA has no sm_107a build, so on R200 the
comparison uses only cuDNN frontend and FLA. Against that baseline,
backward is faster on all 24 backward rows on all three GPUs. fwd+bwd
and ckpt are faster on all but 5 of 48 rows on B200 (worst 0.975x), all
but 1 of 48 on GB300 (0.995x) and all but 2 of 48 on R200 (both ckpt,
0.985x and 0.993x). The forward alone is still slower than cuDNN
frontend (ck0) on all 24 forward rows on B200 and GB300 and on 22 of 24
on R200. Overall, the kernel is faster than the fastest non-Cake
implementation on 67 of 96 rows on B200, up from 55, on 71 of 96 on
GB300, up from 62, and on 72 of 96 on R200, up from 70.

Times are the median CUPTI kernel time with L2 flushed. Main and this PR
ran in alternating fresh processes on the same GPU (ABBA), and the
non-Cake baselines ran separately on the same GPU model. "vs" columns
are baseline ms / this PR ms, so values above 1 mean this PR is faster.
Fastest non-Cake is the best per row of cuDNN frontend 1.32.2
`gated_delta_net` (ckN = checkpoint_every_n_tokens N, bi =
batch_invariant), FLA 0.6.0 `chunk_gated_delta_rule` and FlashQLA 0.1.3
(no sm_107a build), all BF16 q/k/v with an FP32 state and bitwise
repeatable. ckpt is a non-reentrant activation checkpoint (2 x forward +
backward). gL spreads per-value-head decay rates from 1e-4 to 1 (slow to
fast decay), and gB uses A_h = exp(U[0, ln 16]) x softplus(normal
noise), the common fast-decay benchmark gates.

Cake also ships the non-deterministic package of this kernel and the
context-parallel (KCP) forms of both, on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [bfa599d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/bfa599dbc0498671a6591994ba2ad6f6ad1c58cf)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T11:53:29Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet): launch before host work on the NoPE backward and RoPE varlen forward; key the NoPE backward by its saved rows (#9227)

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_train` contains the
non-deterministic Cake training kernels for DeepSeek Sparse Attention.
They implement top-k sparse MLA with absorbed queries and use 64 query
heads and BF16 inputs and outputs, plus an optional FP32 trainer dKV
accumulator. They accumulate dK / dV in FP32 with unordered atomics. The
kernels come in two forms: RoPE (query / key 576 = 512 latent + 64 rope,
value 512) and NoPE (query / key / value 512). Each form has a forward
and a backward. 14 kernel libraries per architecture (built from ten
kernel sources) cover the packed-576 and pre-256 query layouts, trainer
dKV accumulation and the dKV destination row map.

This PR changes only the host (Python) path. The kernels are the same as
on main, and so are their launch parameters, except in the `save_on_cpu`
case below, where main ran a plan baked for the other step's row layout.
- The NoPE autograd backward predicts its binding while the forward runs
and launches its first stage before it allocates the rest of its
buffers.
- The RoPE varlen entry looks up its binding first and launches before
the autograd node is set up.
- Launches whose operands are torch tensors no longer enter an FFI
stream context: tvm-ffi already runs each such call on torch's current
stream. The NoPE forward's index-preparation route (its stage launch and
the pre-bound forward launches over converted tvm-ffi views, issued back
to back in one context) and the prepared runner keep the context.
- The NoPE backward keys its plan by the index rows it reads. A
saved-tensor hook such as `save_on_cpu` returns a saved column slice or
offset view as a contiguous tensor at offset 0, so the backward reads a
different row layout than the forward; that step now gets its own plan.
On main, the second step of each eager / offloaded pair got wrong dq /
dkv (8 of 16 steps in a B200 reproduction); with this PR, 0 of 16.
- The RoPE varlen stage route checks a caller `topk_length` (a
contiguous int32 `[T]` tensor on the rows' device) before any launch.
- The RoPE and NoPE backward binding keys hold the segment class (one
segment, or more than one) instead of the segment count, so a varlen
training step with a new document count reuses the previous backward
binding instead of planning anew.

The tables compare this PR with three references. The first is the
previous Cake version, FlashInfer main bc47d043c (this PR's base),
measured as a same-GPU A/B with interleaved processes (columns main ms,
vs main, A/A band). The second is the deterministic Cake package
`flashinfer.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_det_train` as merged in #9161
(unchanged on main bc47d043c and in this PR), timed in the same
processes (det Cake ms, vs det). The third is, per row, the fastest
non-Cake baseline among those measured (fastest non-Cake, its ms, vs
non-Cake). Forward rows use the fastest of all baselines. bwd, step and
ckpt rows use the fastest baseline that accumulates dK / dV in FP32 as
Cake does (FA4 sparse-MLA); cuDNN, FA4 and FlashMLA + cuDNN write BF16
dK / dV. On `doc_4096` and `doc_16384`, which have no dKV accumulator,
Cake and FA4 sparse-MLA also return BF16 dK / dV (accumulated in FP32);
there cuDNN is faster than Cake on R200 bwd / step (0.917x-0.971x, see
the notes). On forward rows, an arm that zero-fills the FP32 dKV
accumulator later than the benchmark's Cake arm (after its forward
kernel, or in its backward) is replaced by its fill-first variant where
one was measured (‡, see the notes). No row on any of the three GPUs is

det Cake: the deterministic Cake package with the same entry point,
layout, inputs and timed boundaries as the PR, timed in the same
processes with alternating order. vs det = det / PR (above 1: the PR is
faster), the median of the per-round paired ratios; [lo–hi] = the lowest
and highest ratio of a single run (one process; the median over its
rounds); (PR x) = the PR's ms in those runs.
§ bwd against det: step - fwd for both packages on every shape (det Cake
ms, vs det and its PR ms). Through the autograd entry, the deterministic
backward reuses a forward buffer as scratch, so a second backward over
one forward runs the forward again, and a directly timed repeated
backward would include it.
ckpt against det: fwd + step of the same round for both packages, paired
per round as on the other rows.

Rows below 1.0 vs non-Cake. These gaps predate this PR.
- `nope_short_1024_k128` fwd vs FlashMLA + cuDNN: B200 0.790, GB300
0.785. R200 has no FlashMLA build. There, Cake is 1.023x vs FA4
sparse-MLA.
- `nope_short_1024_k128` bwd / step vs FA4 sparse-MLA: B200 0.765 /
0.744, R200 0.950 / 0.866, GB300 step 0.954 (GB300 bwd is 1.034). The
ckpt rows of this shape include the step time and are also below 1.0
(B200 0.987, R200 0.893, GB300 0.974).
- The bwd / step gap comes from the timing boundary. Cake is timed
through its autograd entry (`Function.apply` + `torch.autograd.grad`),
so the engine hands the backward to the device's autograd thread inside
the timed span. The FA4 sparse-MLA arm calls its forward and sparse-MLA
backward functions directly, without autograd. A matched-boundary arm
runs the same two FA4 calls inside a `torch.autograd.Function`, does the
same FP32 dV fill first and is timed the same way. Against it (8
processes per arm), Cake vs FA4 sparse-MLA is:
- B200: bwd 0.377 vs 0.481 ms (1.278x), step 0.408 vs 0.504 ms (1.237x).
- R200: bwd 0.1241 vs 0.1575 ms (1.269x), step 0.1451 vs 0.1724 ms
(1.188x).
- GB300: bwd 0.2553 vs 0.3605 ms (1.412x), step 0.3157 vs 0.4057 ms
(1.285x).
- On the B200 node (Xeon Platinum 8568Y+, C6 exit latency 290 us
enabled, menu governor), waking the autograd thread adds about 0.2 ms
inside the span in some processes. This explains the wide A/A bands on
these B200 rows and why their PR ms and vs non-Cake disagree: Cake had
the delay in 4 of the 8 FA4 sparse-MLA processes (bwd 0.530x-0.538x,
step 0.522x-0.535x) and not in the other 4 (bwd 0.992x-1.049x, step
0.954x-0.971x), and the paired medians 0.765x / 0.744x fall between the
two groups. With the backward on the calling thread
(`torch.autograd.set_multithreading_enabled(False)`), Cake's bwd is
0.171-0.175 ms in 27 / 27 runs vs about 0.200 ms for FA4 sparse-MLA
(about 1.16x), and step is 0.196 vs 0.218 ms.
- GB300 `tail_2123x67923` fwd vs FA4 sparse-MLA (in-place dKV) as
originally placed: Cake 0.672 vs 0.578 ms (0.860x). That arm zero-fills
the FP32 dKV accumulator inside its timed forward but after its kernel,
so its host work before the kernel lies outside the span; the
benchmark's Cake arm fills first, so Cake's host work after the fill
lies inside it. Against the fill-first variant (the ‡ row), Cake is
1.104x. On the other ‡ rows where an arm that fills later is faster than
the ‡ arm, Cake is at parity or faster against the fastest such arm
(1.009x-1.788x; the lowest, GB300 `repro8949_rope` 1.009x and B200
`tail_2123x67923` 1.012x, are parity).
- BF16 dK / dV backwards are report-only and not in the tables. The ones
faster than Cake: cuDNN on R200 `doc_4096` / `doc_4097` / `doc_16384` /
`repro8949_rope` / `repro8949_nope` bwd (0.917x-0.984x) and `doc_4096` /
`doc_16384` step (0.960x-0.971x; on these two rows Cake's dK / dV are
BF16 too), cuDNN on B200 `repro8949_rope` bwd (0.964x), and cuDNN and
FlashMLA + cuDNN on the bimodal B200 `nope_short_1024_k128` bwd / step
rows.

With the customer script from issue #8949 (main / PR, median over runs),
the ratios are 0.9998-1.0013 on GB300 and 1.0021-1.0079 on R200
(parity). On B200 they are 1.011x / 1.007x (RoPE forward / reverse) and
1.019x / 1.019x (NoPE forward / reverse); only the RoPE forward runs do
not overlap (PR 4.865-4.897 ms, main 4.923-4.943 ms), so the other three
are within run-to-run noise.

- Software: CUDA 13.4 (kernels JIT-compiled with nvcc 13.4.2), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130, cuDNN 9.24.0, cuDNN frontend 1.32.2, flash-attn-4
4.0.0b38, FlashMLA 395cb3af (d_qk 512). There is no FlashMLA build on
R200.
- R200 rows were measured on VR200 nodes (212 SMs).
- Timing:
- Each call is timed as a CUPTI span from first to last GPU activity, in
eager mode. L2 is flushed before each call (cold L2).
- Per process, the time is the median over rounds of the per-round
median call.
- main ms / PR ms is the median over processes: 2 main and 4 or 5 PR
processes per row. main, PR and A/A processes are interleaved on one GPU
in ABBA quads (for example main / PR / PR / A/A, then PR / main / A/A /
PR). det Cake uses 8 processes of 10 rounds per row, and the shown
non-Cake baseline 2 to 26 processes per row.
- A/A band: the largest of the max/min spread of the main processes, of
the PR processes and of the A/A processes, and the offset between the
main and A/A medians. The A/A tree is a byte copy of main with its own
JIT caches, timed in the same interleaving. The band is a lower bound on
run-to-run noise.
- vs main = main ms / PR ms. vs non-Cake is the median over the baseline
processes of non-Cake time / Cake time within each process (paired). > 1
means this PR is faster. Against main, a row is faster or slower only
beyond its A/A band. Other ratios within about 1 % of 1.0 are parity. A
vs det ratio whose [lo–hi] run range contains 1.0 (lowest: B200
`packed_glm_a` fwd 0.988x [0.955–1.008]) is within run-to-run noise.
- step = forward + backward. ckpt is the checkpointed training step (2 x
forward + backward), computed as the fwd + step medians. Its non-Cake
column sums the same baseline's fwd and step times, so the ratio is not
paired. Its band is the larger of the fwd and step bands.
- ‡: the fill-first baseline arm. It allocates and zero-fills the
caller's FP32 dKV accumulator at the beginning of its timed forward, as
the benchmark's Cake arm does before it calls the Cake entry. On RoPE
rows the other FA4 sparse-MLA arms fill after their forward kernel, and
public FA4 fills in its backward; on NoPE rows Cake and every baseline
zero-fill their FP32 dK / dV buffer in the timed backward. On forward
rows both sides pay the same fill at the same point. On bwd and step
rows, ‡ marks the fill-first arm where its median ms is the lowest; on
ckpt rows, where its fwd + step sum is the lowest.
- Baselines:
  - cuDNN: cuDNN frontend DSA sparse attention plans (BF16 dK / dV).
  - FA4: flash-attn-4 public sparse attention (BF16 dK / dV).
- FA4 sparse-MLA: the flash-attn-4 forward plus its sparse-MLA backward,
with FP32 dK / dV buffers. On rows with the FP32 dKV accumulator they
are accumulated into it ("in-place dKV" means it writes directly into
views of the accumulator); on `doc_4096` and `doc_16384` they are
returned in BF16, as Cake's are.
- FlashMLA + cuDNN: FlashMLA sparse forward plus the cuDNN backward
(NoPE rows only; the d_qk 576 RoPE build was not measured in these
runs).

Cake also ships the deterministic package
`flashinfer.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_det_train` with the same entry
points; the family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [ebb26db](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ebb26dbdc7278bca289c0e2f3799bc7d4422e307)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T11:30:51Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_det_train): pipelined backward routes for H 2048, H 4096 and H 6144 on SM100 and SM103 (#9217)

The Cake deterministic RMSNorm training kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_det_train`) has variants by input form (2-D
rows, strided rows, per-head 3-D q/k inputs), weight precision (BF16
activations with a BF16 or an FP32 weight) and fused form (plain, or
residual-add fused), each with a forward and a backward. This PR
delivers pipelined backward routes for plain H 2048, H 4096 and H 6144
on sm_100a and sm_103a. On sm_100a they cover H 2048 at T = 1024, 4096,
14928, 16172, 16231, 16384 and 32768, H 4096 at T = 4096 and 14928 to
32768, and H 6144 at T = 1024 and 4096 (22 shape rows on B200 and on
GB200); on sm_103a they cover H 2048 at T = 256, 1024, 4096, 14928,
16172, 16231 and 16384, H 4096 at the same T as on sm_100a, and H 6144
at T = 64, 256, 1024 and 4096 (24 shape rows on GB300). On those rows,
the largest speedup over the current main version of the same kernel is
1.157x on B200, 1.155x on GB200 and 1.167x on GB300 for the backward,
and 1.104x, 1.109x and 1.106x for the training step; the forward is
unchanged everywhere, and the sm_107a routes are unchanged (they use the
same programs as main).

The non-deterministic version of this kernel
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_nondet_train`) and the SiLU-gated RMSNorm
training kernels (`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`,
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_nondet_train`) are not changed here;
the family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

Measured on NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), NVIDIA GB200 (sm_100a, 152
SMs), NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) and dlcluster VR200 (212 SMs), an
sm_107a GPU whose driver reports the name "NVIDIA Graphics Device", with
PyTorch 2.14.1 with CUDA 13.0 and nvcc 13.4.92. Each latency is the
median CUPTI time of one CUDA-graph replay with L2 flushed before each
replay, and speedup = main / PR (above 1 means the PR is faster). Each
table keeps all 143 shape rows.

Shape labels: H is the hidden size and T the token (row) count. `bf16`
means BF16 activations with a BF16 weight, `f32` means an FP32 weight
with BF16 activations, `res` is the residual-add fused form, `(row
stride 576)` is a strided-row input, and `k[T,4,256]` / `q[T,24,256]
strided` are per-head 3-D inputs. Ops: `bwd` is the backward and `step`
is a training step. This PR does not change forward-only latency.

forward+backward and training step) are posted as four comments on this

---------

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [a157b2e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a157b2e6cf2be64755a933671676855dba12989d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T11:16:02Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_nondet): faster non-deterministic training forward and backward (#9182)

Cake's SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel, `y = rmsnorm(x) * w *
silu(z)` (BF16, head dim 128), has 8 variants: deterministic or not,
packed or strided layout, and BF16 or FP32 dw. This PR gives the 4
non-deterministic variants
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_nondet_train`: packed and strided
layouts, BF16 and FP32 dw) new forward and backward programs and new
per-shape routing. The tables cover the packed layout only: 17 shapes T
x H (T tokens, H heads of head dim 128) and 5 operations, so 85 rows per
GPU. Over those rows, the per-GPU geomean speedup ranges from 1.097x
(GB300) to 1.140x (B200) over the previous non-deterministic package on
FlashInfer main ("previous nondet"), and from 1.205x (R200) to 1.238x
(B200) over the fastest non-Cake implementation ("best non-Cake").
Against the deterministic package ("Cake det") as measured before #9223,
it ranges from 1.010x (R200) to 1.037x (B200) and many rows are slower;
#9223 merged after these runs and would lower the backward and step
ratios at the 8 shapes from 8192 x 48 to 65536 x 48.

| GPU | vs previous nondet (A/B) | vs Cake det (before #9223) | vs best
non-Cake |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B200 | 1.140 [0.980, 1.419]; 83 faster, 1 within noise, 1 slower |
1.037 [0.909, 1.588]; 36 faster, 12 equal, 37 slower | 1.238 [0.951,
2.908]; 78 faster, 3 equal, 4 slower |
| GB300 | 1.097 [0.974, 1.377]; 78 faster, 6 within noise, 1 slower |
1.029 [0.912, 1.377]; 45 faster, 14 equal, 26 slower | 1.206 [0.992,
2.434]; 83 faster, 1 equal, 1 slower |
| R200 | 1.131 [0.990, 1.409]; 82 faster, 3 within noise, 0 slower |
1.010 [0.890, 1.418]; 36 faster, 7 equal, 42 slower | 1.205 [0.975,
2.696]; 77 faster, 2 equal, 6 slower |

Each cell gives the geomean [min, max] over the 85 rows, then counts. In
the A/B column, a row is "faster" or "slower" only if it is beyond the
noise band in both passes; otherwise it is "within noise". The noise
band comes from an A/A twin: a second copy of previous nondet timed in
the same run. In the other two columns, "faster", "equal" and "slower"
compare the two-pass mean ratio with 1.000 at three decimals, with no
noise band.

- **vs previous nondet (A/B).** Beyond the noise band, one row is slower
on B200 (1 x 48 backward, BF16 dw, 0.991) and one on GB300 (1 x 48
checkpointed step, FP32 dw, 0.981). R200 has none. The lowest ratios are
within noise: 0.980 on B200 and 0.974 on GB300 (both 129 x 48
checkpointed step, FP32 dw), and 0.990 on R200 (1 x 48 backward, BF16
dw). Even so, one pass at those rows was 0.968 (B200), 0.935 (GB300) and
0.961 (R200).
- **vs Cake det.** The FP32-dw checkpointed step is slower than Cake det
at 14 of 17 shapes on every GPU (all but 1 x 48, 7 x 48 and 512 x 48),
from 0.890 to 0.998. Forward rows are slower at 16 (B200), 9 (GB300) and
17 (R200) of 34. The worst are 0.926 to 0.952, at 1031 x 48 (B200,
R200), 512 x 48 (R200) and 4097 x 16 (GB300); the others are 0.970 or
above. Every BF16-dw backward or step row that is slower than Cake det
is within 0.8% (0.992 to 0.999).
- **vs best non-Cake.** Every equal or slower row is a forward row at T
<= 129, where torch.compile or its Inductor kernel is fastest. The
lowest two-pass mean is 0.951 (B200 129 x 48 forward, CUDA graph). The
lowest single pass is 0.937 (B200 7 x 48 forward, eager). Every backward
and checkpointed-step row is faster in the two-pass mean. Four rows with
a mean above 1 still carry † (best non-Cake equaled or beat new in one
pass). They are the CUDA-graph forward at GB300 1 x 48 and R200 512 x 48
(both 1.009), and the FP32-dw step at R200 64 x 48 (one pass 0.971, mean
1.004) and GB300 1 x 48. At GB300 1 x 48, torch.compile max-autotune
took 6.560 µs in one pass (ratio 0.958) and 9.776 µs in the other. The
mean ratio is therefore 1.193, and the row counts as faster.

**How to read the tables.** Each row is one operation at one
packed-layout shape T x H; the checkpointed step is 2 x forward +
backward. "new" is this PR's package, and each ratio is baseline time /
new time on the same GPU model at the same precision, so a value above 1
means this PR is faster. Times are CUPTI kernel times with a cold L2
from the GPU timer in `flashinfer.testing`, each the median of per-round
medians. "Cake det us", "best non-Cake us" and "new us" are the mean of
two 8-round passes and give det / new and non-Cake / new; † marks a row
where best non-Cake equaled or beat new in at least one pass. The (A/B)
columns come from a separate interleaved run against previous nondet (2
passes x 8 rounds, alternating arm order), so "new us" and "new us
(A/B)" are separate measurements of the same programs. They differ by up
to 1.20x at T <= 129 (GB300 1 x 48 forward, eager), by up to 1.05x at
512 x 48 and 1031 x 48, and by at most 1.023x from T = 4097. Best
non-Cake is, per row, the fastest of torch.compile from PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130 (default and max-autotune, with autograd or no grad), the
Inductor kernel from that PyTorch launched directly (forward only),
vLLM's `layer_norm_fwd_kernel` (vLLM commit 1ecc9cc4, forward only), FLA
0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated` / `rmsnorm_fn`, and mamba_ssm 2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn`;
these are all the same-precision public implementations of this fused op
we found. Cake det is the deterministic package on FlashInfer main
before #9223, which merged after these runs. Per #9223's own tables (not
re-measured here), against current main the det / new ratios at the 8
shapes from 8192 x 48 to 65536 x 48 would be up to 1.07x lower for
backward and up to 1.04x lower for the BF16-dw checkpointed step (#9223
does not time an FP32-dw step), so this PR's backward and step rows
there would match or trail current Cake det.

### [a26550b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a26550be61272e79afdfd2088b5da05c6aa8dc34)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T10:50:48Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_hopper_msa): sm_90a top-k keeps saturated-floor and NaN scores selectable (#9243)

cake_hopper_msa ships 89 sm_90a programs in FlashInfer: sparse decode
attention (22 routes), sparse prefill attention (6), proxy-score decode
(24), proxy-score prefill (5) and top-k block select (32). This PR
re-generates all 32 top-k select programs to fix a correctness bug.
Before this change, a valid block whose score saturated to the float
floor (-2^127 or lower) was dropped as if it were invalid. Now NaN and
any score at or below -2^127 rank as -2^127 and stay selectable. A raw
-inf block stays invalid unless it is a forced block.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of the same programs on
FlashInfer main. This PR is not a speedup. Most rows are slightly
slower. Over the 28 shapes, speedup ranges from 0.937x to 1.017x, with a
geometric mean of 0.986x. 19 rows are more than 0.5 % slower and 2 rows
are more than 0.5 % faster. The rest are within 0.5 %. The two slowest
rows use the per-token valid pages + forced blocks form at 256 tokens:
0.937x (h=1, 2048 blocks) and 0.938x (h=4, 512 blocks). This slowdown is
the cost of the fix.

NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (sm_90a), CUDA 13.4. Median per-call kernel time
from CUPTI (32 ns resolution). Previous and new programs ran interleaved
in both orders, 3 groups x 128 iterations after 8 warm-up. Speedup =
previous / new, so above 1 means this PR is faster. An A/A check on 4
shapes read 0.989x to 1.000x, which is the noise floor.

### [6f97c47](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6f97c4762b9befaa06e88a886a833ded21b7a0a6)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T10:44:52Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc_nondet): SM107 bwd fn split waits for the token-owner pass in its last CTA only (#9235)

Cake ships the mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections) training op
as two modules with the same forward, backward and checkpointed-step
verbs: deterministic `flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train` and
non-deterministic `flashinfer.cake_mhc_nondet_train`. Both run over four
residual streams with BF16 X [T, 4, H], FP32 fn [24, 4H], and FP32
scale, base and their gradients. This PR changes only the
non-deterministic backward on SM107 (R200, sm_107a). Its fn split kernel
runs beside the token-owner pass as its programmatic dependent, and now
only its last CTA waits for that pass. The other CTAs exit after their
split work, so the column-slab pass becomes resident about 12 us before
the token-owner pass ends; outputs are bit-identical to main, and the
sm_100a and sm_103a kernels and routes are unchanged. On R200 at H =
4096, compared with the non-deterministic module on FlashInfer main
(this PR's base), the backward is 1.0057-1.0092x and the checkpointed
step 1.0039-1.0054x faster, with the forward at parity (1.0000-1.0005);
compared with the deterministic module, the backward is 1.0058-1.0143x
and the checkpointed step 1.0107-1.0167x faster. Compared with the
strongest non-Cake implementation timed in the same run, this PR is
1.189-1.226x faster in the forward, 5.262-5.383x in the backward and
8.328-8.450x in the checkpointed step on R200. On GB300 it is
1.198-1.208x, 4.080-4.106x and 3.192-3.211x faster, and also
1.0322-1.0398x (backward) and 1.0200-1.0214x (checkpointed step) faster
than the deterministic module.

This PR's sm_103a kernels and routes are byte-identical to main, so on
GB300 the main/new column compares two loads of the same binary and
measures only the timing harness, as the forward rows show: they run
identical kernels in both columns and have the same spread.

**GB200 (sm_100a):** pending.

Times are microseconds per operation at H = 4096 with four residual
streams. T is the token count, and the checkpointed step is 2 x forward
+ backward. Every ratio is baseline time / this PR's time, so values
above 1 mean this PR is faster. "Cake non-det, main" is the
non-deterministic module on FlashInfer main (this PR's base), and "Cake
det" is the deterministic module. These two and this PR were timed in
the same process on the same GPU with CUDA graph replay and a 512 MiB L2
flush. Each value is the mean over processes of per-process medians, and
A/A noise is that harness's same-binary spread for the row. The last
four columns come from a separate harness that timed the named non-Cake
implementation and this PR in the same process, using CUPTI GPU active
time with an L2 flush over 8 groups x 32 iterations. In that harness,
non-Cake/new is the median over groups of the per-group ratio, and no
ratio mixes the two harnesses. Both GPUs use CUDA 13.4 and PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.

Cake's other variant of this kernel is the deterministic module
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train`, which ships the same forward, backward
and checkpointed-step verbs, including H 5120 and 7168 on sm_107a; the
non-deterministic module ships H 4096, 5120 and 7168 on sm_100a and
sm_103a and H 4096 on sm_107a.

### [06b6546](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/06b65461bd7a0122dc89d0cd94cffa3b3a8c4c39)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T10:34:04Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_latent_moe): faster Kimi-K3 LatentMoE TP8 decode tail on GB200 and GB300 (#9176)

This PR updates the Cake routes for the Kimi-K3 Stable LatentMoE tail
projection of one rank in `flashinfer.experimental.kimi_k3_latent_moe`
(BF16, `sm_100a` and `sm_103a`). The package has four variants: the
front and the tail projection, each for TP1 and TP8. This PR changes
only routes in the TP8 decode tail and makes no program changes. Five
route cells change on the 152-SM parts. On NVIDIA GB200 (`sm_100a`),
they are one token with two routed partials, and two tokens with two or
three routed partials. NVIDIA GB300 (`sm_103a`) already takes this
instance for one token with two partials. On GB300, the changed cells
are two tokens with two or three partials. These cells now take the
existing staged-rows resident-B tail instance, which stages the routed
partial rows in shared memory. Outputs stay bitwise identical to those
of the route each cell took before. Routes on B200 and B300 do not
change. The baseline is the Cake programs on FlashInfer main as of #8340
("previous"). Speedup = previous / this PR. When the tail is timed
alone, the speedup is 1.21x to 1.27x on GB300 and 1.23x to 1.38x on
GB200. With no preceding work, it is 1.28x on GB300 and 1.30x to 1.37x
on GB200. Right after the front projection, it is 1.07x on GB300 and
1.07x to 1.11x on GB200.

| TP | Tokens | Partials | Preceding work | GB300 previous (µs) | GB300
this PR (µs) | GB300 speedup | GB200 previous (µs) | GB200 this PR (µs)
| GB200 speedup |
|--:|--:|--:|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 8 | 1 | 2 | — | — | — | — | 10.576 | 7.672 | 1.38x |
| 8 | 1 | 2 | none | — | — | — | 10.864 | 7.902 | 1.37x |
| 8 | 1 | 2 | front | — | — | — | 28.264 | 25.470 | 1.11x |
| 8 | 2 | 2 | — | 10.080 | 7.936 | 1.27x | 10.304 | 7.896 | 1.30x |
| 8 | 2 | 2 | none | 10.704 | 8.376 | 1.28x | 10.752 | 8.262 | 1.30x |
| 8 | 2 | 2 | front | 28.384 | 26.636 | 1.07x | 28.224 | 26.454 | 1.07x
|
| 8 | 2 | 3 | — | 10.320 | 8.560 | 1.21x | 10.208 | 8.296 | 1.23x |

*Times are µs per call on one rank. Under Preceding work, "—" means the
tail is timed alone, "none" means it runs right after no predecessor
work, and "front" means it runs right after the front projection. Each
value is the median over 8 measurement units. In each unit, both
programs ran interleaved in groups over two passes, with the second pass
in reversed order. "previous" is the median of the previous program's
group times. For rows timed alone it uses the first pass, and for the
other rows it uses both passes. "This PR" adds the paired per-group
difference, averaged over the two passes, to the unit's "previous"
value. A "—" in the GB300 columns means this PR does not change that
GB300 route. Speedup = previous / this PR. Hardware: NVIDIA GB300
(`sm_103a`, 152 SMs) and NVIDIA GB200 (`sm_100a`, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4.*

Cake also ships a TP12 fused tail of this block in `kimi_k3_tp12_tail`;
both packages are BF16 only and target `sm_100a` and `sm_103a`.

### [3bb1e9c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3bb1e9c9a4095186e5561953b30f9cad38913fa7)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T10:10:56Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): add BF16 paged-context sink and LSE programs without tail-order code (#9236)

The Cake FMHA BF16 paged-context kernel (`context_bf16`) handles prefill
with head dim 128, bottom-right causal masking and HND pages. In main,
each module has 60 programs for sm_100a and sm_103a. There are 54
runtime-size programs: six forms times nine GQA packs (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7,
8, 12, 16). There are also six fixed-shape programs. This PR adds 16
programs, for 76 in total. They are the causal + sink and causal + LSE
runtime-size programs of packs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 12, built without
the tail-order code. Eight of them build for both targets and eight
build for sm_103a only. Pack 16 keeps its current programs.

- The new programs do not read bit 31 of `full_sections` on each launch.
Their tail units always run one after another, and `full_sections` is
the plain section count.
- Host routing in `flashinfer/cake_fmha.py` sends a causal sink or LSE
launch to the new program of its pack when three conditions hold: the
modelled tail order is plain, the target ships that program, and
`max_kv_len` is within the target's bound. The bound is 1024 keys on
sm_100a (B200) and 4096 keys on sm_103a (GB300). All other launches keep
the current programs.
- Tiles, rows, key blocks and arithmetic do not change. Output and LSE
stay bitwise equal to main and to the JIT module. Existing program names
and bytes do not change.

The baseline is the previous Cake version: FlashInfer main without this
PR. On B200, 15 rows of at most 1024 keys are faster than main by
1.0062x-1.0264x. On GB300, 16 rows of at most 4096 keys are faster than
main by 1.0069x-1.0444x. Three B200 rows and 20 GB300 rows tie main, and
this PR claims no gain on them. No row is slower than main beyond the
noise floor, and every row is faster than the JIT module.

### [36718d1](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/36718d11b56929241e6fd327659bb8198124686e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T09:53:53Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): faster FP8 context LSE, sink and non-causal forms on B200 and GB300 (#9231)

Cake FMHA paged-context attention in `flashinfer.cake_fmha` (FP8 E4M3,
head dim 128) has 6 forms, 9 GQA packs, 2 program kinds and 2 scale
kinds. The forms are causal, non-causal, causal + LSE, causal + sink,
non-causal + LSE and non-causal + sink. The packs are 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7,
8, 12 and 16. The program kinds are runtime-size programs and one-stage
programs for short queries. The scale kinds are host-scalar and
device-tensor dequantization scales. This PR changes the five non-plain
forms in every pack. The plain causal form keeps its routes. The
baseline is the previous Cake version: FlashInfer main without this PR.
On B200, one-stage rows are 1.421x-1.492x faster than main (8 rows) and
two-stage swapped-P-tile rows are 1.030x-1.059x faster (13 rows). On
GB300, one-stage rows are 1.267x-1.300x faster (8 rows). Each row was
faster than main in all 10 memory layouts. Output and LSE are bitwise
equal to the JIT module.

- **Swapped P tile on B200.** sm_100a now runs the two-stage form
programs with the 4-stage K/V ring. Each stage's P tile is held in the
other stage's S columns, as sm_103a already does. Launches of at most
128 keys keep the 3-stage programs.
- **One-stage route for packs 1, 2, 4 and 8.** A call with more than 128
keys now takes the one-stage program of its pack on both targets when
its tiles fit one wave. The condition is batch x (query heads / pack) x
ceil(query length / (128 / pack)) <= SM count (148 on B200, 152 on
GB300).

based on input and hardware characteristics, including additional pack
choices.

applicable architectures, while retaining the existing single-stage path
on others.

### [47cef9f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/47cef9f60cfee5a1db8fd1e693b34ff6257d75df)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T09:34:31Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train): keep the serpentine K walk out of program knobs (#9241)

`cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train` derives the deterministic planner's knobs
for a program from the deterministic package's symbol inverse
(`_template_knobs`). Since #9170 that inverse also returns the
serpentine K walk `kser`, which
`cake_dense_gemm_det_train_projection_plan()` does not take as a
keyword. On main, every row this package plans through a deterministic
program (input-gradient rules, nvjet rows, forward program entries,
weight-gradient rules) therefore raises `TypeError`.

This change drops `kser` when it is 0, which gives these rows the knobs
they had before #9170. A program with a nonzero `kser` is planned only
by the deterministic package's own rules, so it raises `ValueError` like
any other symbol without planner knobs. A new CPU test checks that every
knob set the package passes to the deterministic planner uses only that
planner's keywords.

No kernel or plan changes: on B200, the 255 bench rows that run on main
launch the same programs with bit-identical outputs, and the 39 rows
that raise on main run again.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* Improved validation of deterministic GEMM training configurations:
unsupported nonzero serial-reduction settings are now rejected, while
zero-valued settings are omitted from planner options. This helps
prevent invalid configurations from being accepted and keeps planner
settings aligned with supported options.

### [cd7898a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cd7898a0efca7629e6ab70823ffdacb9e7d61587)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T09:31:31Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_causal_conv1d_det_train): SM-wide row-group backward for C 520-615 from per-arch token floors (#9240)

`flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_det_train` is the deterministic packed
width-4 depthwise causal convolution + SiLU training forward/backward
(BF16 activations `[S, C]`, documents delimited by `cu_seqlens`). Every
output repeats bit for bit from run to run. The forward has three
configurations (FP32 taps, BF16 taps, with bias); the backward has five.
This PR changes only the default backward (FP32 taps, no bias, default
SiLU' policy) on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. The forward and the other
four backward configurations are unchanged. On `main`, single-tile rows
with C 520–615 (C 520–687 on sm_107a) run 32-channel-vector tiles, and
the last tile is partly empty. These rows now switch to the package's
existing SM-wide row-group backward program once S reaches a
per-architecture token floor: 65,536 on sm_100a, 24,576 on sm_103a and
32,768 on sm_107a. That program runs one CTA per SM, with one whole
channel tile per CTA. Below the floor and at larger C, the SM-wide
program is slower, so the previous programs still run those rows. Only
the host-side program selection changes; the kernels are unchanged. On
the changed rows, the backward is 1.19–1.34x faster than `main` on B200,
1.17–1.31x on GB300 and 1.04–1.15x on R200. The forward + backward step
is 1.12–1.27x, 1.12–1.38x and 1.07–1.10x faster. The checkpointed step
is 1.08–1.21x, 1.08–1.28x and 1.05–1.07x faster. The forward column
reads 1.000x on every changed row. All other rows run the same programs
as `main` and read 0.993x–1.009x on B200, 0.998x–1.003x on GB300 and
0.995x–1.004x on R200. Five of these same-program cells (two on B200,
three on R200) read slightly below their A/A band in this run, but each
read within its band when re-measured, and the tables keep the first-run
values.

**B200** (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1 (CUDA 13.0
runtime). Each cell: `main → this PR` latency in µs, then (speedup =
`main` latency / this PR's latency, > 1 means this PR is faster; A/A ±
noise band, the half-width of the per-round range of a second copy of
the `main` package timed against `main`). Forward and backward: CUPTI
GPU time of the phase's kernels, cold L2. Forward + backward step (one
forward plus one backward) and checkpointed step (two forwards plus one
backward under activation checkpointing): L2 flushed, call queued behind
a spin kernel, timed with CUDA events. 12 interleaved rounds in each of
two runs, with the two versions' positions swapped between the runs;
latency is the geometric mean of the two runs' medians.

`flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_nondet_train` (with its context-parallel
entry) also exists, and the whole family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
* Backward processing now supports additional channel-size ranges across
several GPU architectures, including larger workloads.

* **Behavior Notes**

slightly from earlier versions. Outputs, input gradients, and documented
accuracy bounds remain unchanged.
* Workspace requirements may be higher for certain channel sizes and
bias configurations.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [0232a8b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0232a8b9aa95f58d30b18699988a62e585667bbc)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T09:13:38Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train): look-ahead backward for long packed rows (#9223)

The Cake SiLU-gated RMSNorm training op (y = RMSNorm(x, w) * SiLU(z),
BF16 x/z/y of shape [T, H, 128], BF16 or FP32 weight gradient) has two
variants, deterministic and non-deterministic. This PR adds a look-ahead
backward for long packed rows to the deterministic
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`. When grad_out, x and z
are packed rows (head stride 128, token stride H * 128) and the call has
at least 2560 rows per SM on sm_100a and sm_103a (1536 on sm_107a), the
backward loads the next block's rows while the current block's row math
runs. It keeps the same grid, the same FP32 operations in the same order
and the same workspace, so dx, dz and dw have the same bits as before.
Both weight-gradient dtypes get the new path. Every other call runs the
unchanged backward, and the forward and the non-deterministic kernels
are unchanged. In these tables, 8192x48 and every larger shape take the
new path on B200 and GB300, and VR200 also uses it for 10185x32. Speedup
over the deterministic package on main on those shapes (Table A, 16
shapes x 5 columns per GPU, 240 cells): backward with a BF16 weight
gradient 1.008-1.069x on B200, 1.004-1.071x on GB300 and 1.005-1.058x on
VR200; backward with an FP32 weight gradient 1.008-1.069x on B200,
1.005-1.071x on GB300 and 1.031-1.057x on VR200; checkpointed step in a
CUDA graph 1.004-1.037x on B200, 1.003-1.033x on GB300 and 1.016-1.028x
on VR200. The one exception is VR200 at 8192x48, where the FP32 backward
and the CUDA-graph checkpointed step are within the A/A band. No cell is
slower beyond the A/A band. The forward is within the band on every
shape, and so is every cell of the shapes that keep the old path. The
host-bound eager checkpointed step is within its wide band except in 4
cells, where it is faster: 65536x48 on B200 (1.035x), 30193x48 and
65536x48 on GB300 (1.020-1.022x) and 30193x48 on VR200 (1.029x). Over
the fastest non-Cake implementation (Table B): faster in all 144 cells
(48 per GPU), 1.021-1.481x. On each GPU the smallest margin is a forward
against TC-MA: 256x48 at 1.021x on VR200 (3.10 vs 3.17 us) and 1.024x on
B200 (4.03 vs 4.13 us), and 8192x48 at 1.038x on GB300 (44.86 vs 46.56
us).

B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), VR200 (sm_107a, 212
SMs); CUDA 13.4.2 (nvcc), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Median
CUPTI time of one call (first kernel start to last kernel end), cold L2,
in us. Table A columns: forward; backward with a BF16 weight gradient;
backward with an FP32 weight gradient accumulated in place
(`accumulate_grad_weight=True`, the main_grad use); checkpointed step (2
x forward + backward) in a CUDA graph; the same step eager. The
checkpointed steps compute a BF16 weight gradient. Table A: main and PR
in separate processes, alternating order main / PR / main', 4 rounds; on
B200 the 256x48, 512x48, 1024x48 and 7986x32 rows are a 12-round
re-measure in every column but the FP32 one. The times are medians over
the rounds and the speedup is the median of the per-round main/PR
ratios, so in the eager column it can differ from the ratio of the two
times. A/A band: the larger of the largest |1 - main/main'| between two
separate main processes and the largest in-process A/A deviation; †
marks a ratio inside it. The eager step's time includes the host gaps
between its kernels, so its band is wide. Table B: fastest of FLA 0.6.0
(rms_norm_gated, layernorm_gated), mamba_ssm 2.3.2 rmsnorm_fn,
torch.compile default (TC, best of 3 fresh compiles) and
max-autotune-no-cudagraphs (TC-MA, best of 2), and a pinned Triton
forward (TRITON). Cake and non-Cake are measured in the same run, 3
rounds; on B200 the same four shapes are a 9-round re-measure. Backward
and the checkpointed step are replayed from CUDA graphs. Table B's
forward compares Cake's forward with a preallocated output against the
fastest non-Cake forward, grad-enabled or under torch.no_grad().

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [b7c1b02](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b7c1b02cf39b3b98978d65e2380b09e42d32f230)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T08:43:40Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_causal_conv1d): faster nondet KCP backward host flow (#9230)

For #8365.

The Cake packed width-4 depthwise causal conv1d + SiLU training kernel
(BF16 activations, FP32 taps, FP32 weight gradient) has four variants:
deterministic and non-deterministic, each in a single-rank form and a
context-parallel (KCP) form. This PR changes only the backward host flow
of the non-deterministic KCP form,
`flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_nondet_train_kcp` (from #9154), and makes
no kernel changes. The backward's main program now sizes its unit of
tokens per shape, and with more than one rank a high-priority side
stream runs the head program, the multi-tensor send-row packing and the
issue of the halo exchange, so the main program begins at once on the
caller's stream. A multi-tensor call whose tensors share one width also
reads its received rows in place and runs the tensors' tail-row programs
concurrently. Unloaded (Table 1), the new ND Cake route is 2.03x-2.22x
faster than best non-Cake in the forward, 6.52x-7.41x in the backward,
4.81x-5.45x in forward + backward and 4.01x-4.67x checkpointed. Its
backward ratio is 1.011x-1.090x against previous ND Cake unloaded and
0.991x-1.110x loaded (Table 2), and 1.005x-1.124x against det Cake
unloaded and 1.006x-1.333x loaded. Forward + backward is 1.007x-1.057x
against previous ND Cake and 1.005x-1.089x against det Cake;
checkpointed is 1.006x-1.041x and 1.006x-1.066x. The B200 CP8
multi-tensor backward rows with 1 SM held or a 1-thread side kernel were
0.981x-0.986x against det Cake in #9154 and are now 1.027x-1.042x (new
vs det: 513.5 vs 527.3 us, 506.6 vs 526.2 us, 505.7 vs 526.8 us). The
rows below 1.000x follow, with times given as new vs baseline. The
forward against previous ND Cake is 0.998x on GB300 C=10240 (244.6 vs
244.2 us), 0.998x on GB300 multi-tensor (318.4 vs 317.8 us), 0.998x on
GB200 C=10240 (266.7 vs 266.2 us) and 0.997x on GB200 multi-tensor
(347.8 vs 346.8 us); this PR does not change the forward, and each gap
is within that GPU's run-to-run spread. The VR200 multi-tensor forward
is 0.991x against det Cake (227.5 vs 225.5 us); both routes launch the
same forward program with the same grid (as #9154 states), the same det
program measured in the two trees of this run differed by 0.73% on this
row, and the gap is at that level. The VR200 C=10240 backward with 16
SMs held is 0.991x against previous ND Cake (246.1 vs 244.0 us); both
routes use the same 64-token plan on this GPU, and the gap is within
VR200's 1.94% run-to-run spread.

*Table 1, unloaded. Per-rank shapes are in the contiguous CP layout
packed into four documents: C=10240 with 32768 tokens/rank as one
tensor, and three C=8192 tensors through the multi-tensor entry with
16384 tokens/rank. GPUs: B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs) at CP8 (8 GPUs); GB200
(sm_100a, 152 SMs), GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) and VR200 (sm_107a, 212
SMs) at CP4. The checkpointed operation is the torch.utils.checkpoint
step (forward, recompute forward, backward). Every time is that of the
slowest rank, measured with CUDA events in eager execution (no CUDA
graphs), with L2 flushed before each sample (cold L2), host enqueue
hidden behind a GPU spin and ranks aligned by an `all_reduce`. On each
GPU, each source tree ran twice on one node in the order new, previous,
previous, new; each run used interleaved rounds with the arm order
rotated each round (7 rounds on B200 and GB300, 5 rounds on GB200 and
VR200). Each Cake time is the median of the round values pooled over
that tree's two runs; det Cake is the det route of the two runs of main.
The largest spread between the two runs of one tree, over all rows of a
GPU, is 0.55% on B200, 0.60% on GB200, 1.30% on GB300 (on a det row; ND
rows at most 0.81%) and 1.94% on VR200 (ND rows; det rows at most
1.34%). Ratios are baseline time / new time; above 1.000x means the new
route is faster. Baselines: previous ND Cake is the non-deterministic
Cake KCP route on FlashInfer main 504db804 (with #9154), before this PR;
det Cake is the deterministic Cake KCP route
`cake_causal_conv1d_det_train_kcp` on the same main 504db804, which this
PR does not change; best non-Cake is, per row, the fastest of FLA 0.6.0
context-parallel conv (FLA-triton is its Triton backend; FLA-cuda and
FLA-cuda-det are its CUDA backend, the Dao causal-conv1d 1.7.0 kernels,
in atomic and deterministic mode), Megatron-Core 0.20.0
`causal_conv1d_cp` (Megatron, Megatron-det) and torch.compile 2.14.1
(default and max-autotune-no-cudagraphs) with an `all_to_all` halo. All
of these compute with BF16 activations and FP32 accumulation and are the
strongest same-precision implementations, deterministic or not. Best
non-Cake times come from the same four runs on B200 (median per
implementation), from a separate run on the same node right after the
four runs on GB200, from the first new run on the same node on VR200,
and on GB300 from an earlier run with the same harness and protocol on
another GB300 node (5 rounds), because the GB300 environment for this
run lacked FLA and Megatron-Core. Software: PyTorch 2.14.1 (CUDA 13.0
runtime); the Cake kernels were built with CUDA 13.4.2.*

FlashInfer also ships the other three Cake variants, the deterministic
KCP form (`cake_causal_conv1d_det_train_kcp`), the single-rank
deterministic form (`cake_causal_conv1d_det_train`) and the single-rank
non-deterministic form (`cake_causal_conv1d_nondet_train`), and the
family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [023a847](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/023a8474e1f7469572c0d4284535fc6ffa699574)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T08:04:46Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gated_act_mxfp8): retune the per-size programs on SM100, SM103 and SM107 (#9226)

`flashinfer.cake_gated_act_mxfp8_det_train` is Cake's deterministic
fused SwiGLU + MXFP8 quantization kernel for training. The forward pass
quantizes `silu(gate) * up` of a BF16 `[M, 2K]` input, and the backward
pass quantizes the gate and up gradients. Each pass writes rowwise,
colwise or both E4M3 outputs, with one E8M0 (RCEIL) scale per 32 values
in the swizzled 128 x 4 layout. The kernel has one data type (BF16 in,
MXFP8 out) and six forms: forward and backward, each writing rowwise,
colwise or both outputs. This PR retunes the per-size programs on SM100,
SM103 and SM107, and each size range now runs the program measured
fastest for it. For small problems, the selected programs use 32-column
tiles with more resident blocks per SM. Narrow 16-lane tiles now cover
more small rowwise sizes on SM100 and SM107. Mid-size forward colwise
problems on SM107 use a 64-column tile. More sizes also use 2-row tiles,
a packed sigmoid or another saturation-band path.

Each table compares this PR with the same module on current FlashInfer
main (the previous Cake version) on the same GPU:

- Build: CUDA 13.4 (nvcc build `cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0`)
and PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.
- Timing: CUPTI kernel time, with L2 flushed before every call.
- Runs: main and the PR are interleaved in one process and timed twice
per run over three runs. Each value is the median of the 6 pooled
samples.
- Shapes (M x K, where K is the output width): the representative shapes
are 128 x 128, 4096 x 2048, 4096 x 7168, 16384 x 7168 and 131072 x 8192.
The other shapes are 256 x 256, 256 x 512, 512 x 512, 512 x 1024, 1024 x
1024, 1024 x 2048, 1536 x 2048, 2048 x 2048, 3072 x 2048, 8192 x 8192,
12288 x 8192 and 32768 x 8192. All three GPUs run the same 17 shapes.
- Inputs: unit normals, and block-scaled (unit normals times a random
power of two in [2^-8, 2^8] per 32-value block).
- Noise band: a result counts as faster or slower only when its speedup
exceeds its noise band. The band is the largest of three values, each
taken relative to main's time. They are the A/A offset (two copies of
main's code measured the same way), main's spread across samples, and 64
ns (two ticks of the CUPTI timer). A result whose program is the same on
both sides is noise by construction. If such a result exceeds its noise
band, the tables mark it "same program (... = noise)".
- Tables: for each GPU, table 1 shows every pass at the representative
shapes. Table 2 shows the other measured shapes, but only the passes
whose program this PR changes. "New program" is "yes" when this PR runs
a different program than main for that cell.

### NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs)

Of the 204 results over 17 shapes, 27 are faster beyond their noise
band, 177 are noise and 0 are slower. This PR changes the program in 31
cells (62 results): 27 are faster, 35 are noise and 0 are slower. The
lowest speedup of any changed result is 0.997x: 256 x 512 bwd both on
unit normals, from 2.75 to 2.76 µs (noise). At the representative
shapes, 1 of the 60 results is faster and 59 are noise. The faster one
is 128 x 128 fwd both on block-scaled inputs, from 2.30 to 2.24 µs
(1.029x). The changed cells there are 128 x 128 fwd colwise, fwd both
and bwd both. The largest speedups are on block-scaled inputs. They are
256 x 256 bwd rowwise from 2.62 to 2.18 µs (1.206x), 512 x 512 fwd
rowwise from 2.88 to 2.53 µs (1.139x), 256 x 512 bwd rowwise from 2.72
to 2.40 µs (1.133x) and 256 x 256 fwd rowwise from 2.52 to 2.24 µs
(1.125x). On unit normals, 256 x 256 bwd rowwise goes from 2.30 to 2.18
µs (1.059x) and 1024 x 2048 fwd rowwise from 4.77 to 4.57 µs (1.044x).

### NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs)

Of the 204 results over 17 shapes, 24 are faster beyond their noise band
and 176 are noise. The other 4 run the same program on both sides but
fall outside their band, so they count as noise. Three of them are
slower, all on block-scaled inputs:

- 8192 x 8192 bwd both, from 103.60 to 103.81 µs (0.998x, noise band
0.06%).
- 32768 x 8192 bwd rowwise, from 303.44 to 306.45 µs (0.990x, noise band
0.09%).
- 32768 x 8192 bwd both, from 393.81 to 394.05 µs (0.999x, noise band
0.02%).

The fourth is faster: 8192 x 8192 bwd rowwise on unit normals, from
80.35 to 80.27 µs (1.001x, noise band 0.08%). This PR changes the
program in 25 cells (50 results): 24 are faster, 26 are noise and 0 are
slower. The lowest speedup of any changed result is 0.990x: 256 x 256
bwd colwise on unit normals, from 2.30 to 2.33 µs (noise). At the
representative shapes, 3 of the 60 results are faster and 57 are noise.
All three faster results are on block-scaled inputs. They are 128 x 128
fwd colwise from 2.06 to 2.00 µs (1.032x), 128 x 128 bwd both from 2.46
to 2.35 µs (1.044x) and 4096 x 7168 bwd rowwise from 39.14 to 38.15 µs
(1.026x). The largest speedups on block-scaled inputs are 1024 x 1024
bwd both from 5.77 to 5.31 µs (1.086x), 512 x 512 bwd colwise from 3.10
to 2.91 µs (1.066x), 12288 x 8192 fwd both from 103.76 to 97.85 µs
(1.060x) and 8192 x 8192 fwd both from 71.54 to 67.90 µs (1.054x). On
unit normals, 1024 x 1024 fwd rowwise goes from 3.23 to 3.17 µs (1.020x)
and 8192 x 8192 fwd both from 62.82 to 62.23 µs (1.010x).

### NVIDIA R200 on a VR NVL4 board (sm_107a)

Of the 204 results over 17 shapes, 49 are faster beyond their noise band
and 153 are noise. The other 2 run the same program on both sides and
are slower beyond their band, so they count as noise:

- 32768 x 8192 bwd both on block-scaled inputs, from 266.53 to 266.78 µs
(0.999x, noise band 0.04%).
- 131072 x 8192 fwd rowwise on unit normals, from 445.02 to 445.09 µs
(1.000x, noise band 0.01%).

This PR changes the program in 34 cells (68 results): 49 are faster, 19
are noise and 0 are slower. The lowest speedup of any changed result is
0.990x: 1024 x 1024 fwd both on unit normals, from 3.20 to 3.23 µs. That
result is noise, under the 64 ns floor. At the representative shapes, 12
of the 60 results are faster and 47 are noise. One is marked same
program: the 131072 x 8192 fwd rowwise result above. This PR changes 9
cells at those shapes. The largest speedups on block-scaled inputs are
512 x 1024 bwd colwise from 3.46 to 2.94 µs (1.174x), 1024 x 1024 bwd
colwise from 4.16 to 3.56 µs (1.168x), 256 x 256 bwd rowwise from 2.53
to 2.24 µs (1.129x) and 1024 x 1024 fwd colwise from 3.58 to 3.18 µs
(1.128x). On unit normals, 2048 x 2048 fwd colwise goes from 5.66 to
5.19 µs (1.091x) and 256 x 256 bwd rowwise from 2.37 to 2.22 µs
(1.065x). At the representative shapes, 4096 x 2048 bwd colwise on
block-scaled inputs goes from 11.10 to 10.56 µs (1.052x). There, 4096 x
7168 bwd colwise on unit normals goes from 26.46 to 26.05 µs (1.016x).

### [e3ebb9e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e3ebb9e7dd2f7a2a4a580ecf69369abaa81ede16)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T07:41:37Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train, cake_dsa_indexer_nondet_train): sm_107a l6 snake ticket program reads its next ticket at the end of each unit (#9218)

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train` is the deterministic DSA indexer
for training. It fuses scoring with exact top-k, keeps ids, scores and
order bitwise identical from run to run, and has BF16-score and
FP8-score variants. Its non-deterministic twin,
`flashinfer.cake_dsa_indexer_nondet_train`, shares the scan programs,
returns the same exact top-k set per row with free slot order, and has a
BF16-score variant only. This PR changes one program in both packages,
the BF16 sm_107a "l6 snake" ticket scan program: its fold warps now read
and acknowledge the next unit's ticket at the end of each unit instead
of right after the unit's Q load, and outputs stay bitwise identical to
main. On R200 only rows S1, S2, S3, V1 and s3_cold16k run this program,
and there the speedup against FlashInfer main (main ms / PR ms; above 1
means the PR is faster) is 1.003x to 1.022x (det) and 1.007x to 1.021x
(nondet). All other R200 rows and every GB300 and B200 row run the same
programs as main, so their ratios are measurement noise: 0.990x to
1.015x (det) and 0.993x to 1.048x (nondet) on R200, 0.992x to 1.011x
(det) and 0.993x to 1.010x (nondet) on GB300, and 0.982x to 1.084x (det)
and 0.983x to 1.043x (nondet) on B200. Against the deterministic Cake
package in the same process (det PR ms / nondet PR ms), the nondet
package measures 1.003x to 1.204x on R200, 1.000x to 1.192x on GB300 and
0.994x to 1.195x on B200 (only doc262k_topic_r14 is below 1, at 0.994x).
Against the fastest same-precision non-Cake baseline per row (cuDNN
frontend 1.32.2 fused score + top-k, cuDNN dense FP32 scores +
`indexer_top_k_wrapper`, or a torch FP32-output GEMM + FlashInfer
deterministic top-k), it measures 1.538x to 36.521x on R200, 1.338x to
36.683x on GB300 and 1.347x to 29.946x on B200, with the lowest ratio at
S1 on every GPU. The non-Cake baselines were measured on only 20
representative rows, in separate runs on the same GPU models, so the
other rows have no non-Cake measurement.

**R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs)**

The det and nondet packages from main and from this PR all run in one
process on the CUDA 13.4 toolkit and torch 2.14.1+cu130. `main` and `PR`
are median one-call latencies in ms from CUPTI kernel time with cold L2
and arm orders AB, BA and interleaved, `speedup` is main ms / PR ms,
`A/A` is the difference from timing the same package twice, `T` is query
rows, `Tkv` key rows, `segments` packed documents, and `ratio` the key
pooling ratio (each key row pools `ratio` query tokens; 1 = no pooling).
Rows marked (r) (S4_peaked, S4sink, V3, V7, Z1k256, s2_4x2k_packed and
doc262k_topic_r09) show the median over 4 rerun rounds (per arm, the
median of the 4 round medians); each round ran 100 calls per arm and
order in a fresh process on a different GPU.

`det Cake (PR)` and `nondet PR` repeat the PR latencies above (same
process, CUDA 13.4 toolkit, torch 2.14.1+cu130), and `vs det Cake` is
det ms / nondet ms. `non-Cake baseline` names the fastest of three
baselines: cuDNN frontend 1.32.2 fused score + top-k
(`indexer_forward_top_k_wrapper`, deterministic=True or False), cuDNN
dense FP32 scores + `indexer_top_k_wrapper` (deterministic), and a torch
FP32-output GEMM + FlashInfer deterministic top-k for rows with top_k
4096, which cuDNN does not support. All three compute the same op with
BF16 Q/K, FP32 weights and FP32 logits, and their timed region includes
converting the output to ascending ids with aligned scores. `baseline
ms` comes from separate runs on the same GPU model with the same CUPTI
cold-L2 timer and arm orders, `vs non-Cake` is baseline ms / nondet PR
ms, and `-` marks rows outside the 20 measured rows.

### [8f344f9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8f344f99d743048439221ef9daac13d775d72884)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T07:36:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): sm_103a NVFP4 paged context drops a redundant proxy fence (#9228)

This PR speeds up the sm_103a (GB300) programs for Cake paged-context
(prefill) attention. This kernel uses an E4M3 query and output with
NVFP4 K/V pages, head dim 128 and bottom-right causal masking. It has 11
programs per target: two fixed-size programs, one with host scalar
scales and one with device scalar scales, and nine runtime-size
programs, one for each GQA pack (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 16). In all
11 programs, the dequant warps no longer issue a redundant proxy fence
after the packed-page ring wait. Outputs are bitwise unchanged. The
sm_100a programs are not changed.

The baseline is the previous Cake version, which is FlashInfer main
without this PR. On GB300, 26 of 28 rows are faster than main in all 10
memory layouts, with speedups (main/new) from 1.004x to 1.033x. Two rows
tie main with no gain: 1 x 128 q / 128 kv with 8/8 heads, and 16 x 512 q
/ 512 kv with 8/1 heads. The new programs beat the JIT module on every
row. trtllm-gen is shown for reference only and is faster than this PR
on some rows.

### GB300 (sm_103a)

driver 580.159.03. Times in microseconds, median of 10 layouts per row
(the page table of each layout comes from its seed).

### [667ba59](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/667ba59e83763e05513108e9ab8a484320f8a638)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T07:34:07Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp): keep the checkpoint hand-off's kept set in a private memory pool (#9193)

Cake ships KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked training as four packages:
deterministic and non-deterministic, each single-rank and with context
parallelism over packed documents (KCP); this PR changes
`cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp`, the non-deterministic KCP package. In a
checkpointed pass of a `workspace=None` call, the checkpoint hand-off's
kept set now comes from a package-private `torch.cuda.MemPool` per
device instead of the caching allocator's default pool, so reserved
memory no longer grows across training steps;
`cake_kcp.default_workspace_cache_clear()` now also drops these pools
(`torch.cuda.empty_cache()` does not release a live pool's free blocks),
calls with a caller-held workspace keep the default pool, and outputs
and gradients are bitwise unchanged. On GB300, compared with FlashInfer
`main` (the previous Cake version of this package), steady-state
reserved memory drops by 4226 to 9162 MiB per rank and the allocated
peak stays within 3 MiB of `main`'s; the pool costs one kept set over
`checkpoint_handoff="off"` (816 MiB here), in the first step the
`handle` rows reserve 354 MiB (`g`) and 202 MiB (`g`, L2 norm) more than
`main` and the raw-gate rows 16 MiB more, and allocating a kept set from
the pool takes within 2 us of the default pool's host time. Only the
checkpointed step's recompute takes the changed path, and fwd, bwd and
fwd+bwd run the same code as `main`; on GB300 (sm_103a) and R200
(sm_107a) no row (5 shapes x 4 ops) is slower than `main` beyond the A/A
band, both with the two packages in one process and with one package per
process, and on GB200 (sm_100a) every fwd, bwd and fwd+bwd row is within
the band. With the two packages in one process, the GB200 checkpointed
step measures `main / PR` 0.996x to 0.999x (this PR slower), with shapes
A and D (0.997x) beyond their 0.2% A/A band, and a second GB200 node
repeated the one-process comparison with the same result; with one
package per process the same rows measure 0.999x to 1.001x, and the
comparisons in #9155 against the deterministic Cake package, FLA 0.6.0
and cuDNN KDA otherwise stand.

Reserved memory per rank (GB300, sm_103a, CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92),
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130; CP4, 64 heads, packs of 65536 tokens; MiB, max
over ranks), first step after `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` and the steady
state of the next 3 steps; "before" = main, "pool" = this PR:

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Checkpointed calls can reuse per-device memory for kept tensors when
enabled and eligible. The new `kept_pool` option controls this behavior
and defaults to enabled.
* Clearing the default workspace cache now also clears kept-tensor pools
and related caches.

* **Documentation**
* Added guidance on kept-tensor pool behavior, lifetime, cleanup, and
memory use, with updated accuracy and determinism results for CP64.

* **Tests**
* Added coverage for pool selection, memory reuse, cache clearing,
option validation, and bitwise equivalence when pooling is disabled.

### [ef35948](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ef359483cdb3b14f3a6517993ea1a255b3bc55e5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T07:29:15Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det_train): forward on the WY stage's A and split forward on long documents (#9204)

`flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train` is the deterministic (bitwise run-to-run
repeatable) chunked gated delta rule training kernel. It runs forward
and backward over variable-length documents and supports activation
checkpointing. It has variants along three axes: BF16 q/k/v with FP32 or
BF16 beta, q/k L2 norm fused into the kernel or done by the caller, and
q/k/v as head views of one packed projection row or as separate
contiguous tensors. This PR delivers the forward for FP32 beta with the
fused q/k L2 norm in two forms: one runs on the WY stage's A matrix, and
the other is a one-wave split forward for long documents. It also trims
host-side bookkeeping. The backward kernels are unchanged. Compared with
main, forward is up to 1.50x faster (B200, gL, H/HV 8/24, 32,768
tokens), fwd+bwd up to 1.12x and ckpt up to 1.22x, and backward stays at
about 1.00x. Some rows are slower than main: 11 of 96 on B200, 19 of 96
on GB300 and 7 of 96 on R200, worst 0.93x (GB300, gB, H/HV 1/3 at
524,288 tokens, forward). Most of these are gB forward rows or small
32,768-token rows bound by host overhead. Compared with the fastest
non-Cake implementation, backward wins on almost every row and fwd+bwd
and ckpt win on most rows. The forward alone is slower than cuDNN
frontend (ck0) on 70 of the 72 forward rows.

Times are the median CUPTI kernel time with L2 flushed. Main and this PR
ran in alternating fresh processes on the same GPU (ABBA), and the
non-Cake baselines ran separately on the same GPU model. "vs" columns
are baseline ms / this PR ms, so values above 1 mean this PR is faster.
Fastest non-Cake is the best per row of cuDNN frontend 1.32.2
`gated_delta_net` (ckN = checkpoint_every_n_tokens N, bi =
batch_invariant), FLA 0.6.0 `chunk_gated_delta_rule` and FlashQLA 0.1.3
(no sm_107a build), all BF16 q/k/v with an FP32 state and bitwise
repeatable. ckpt is a non-reentrant activation checkpoint (2 x forward +
backward). gL spreads per-value-head decay rates from 1e-4 to 1 (slow to
fast decay), and gB uses A_h = exp(U[0, ln 16]) x softplus(normal
noise), the common fast-decay benchmark gates.

Cake also ships the non-deterministic package of this kernel and the
context-parallel (KCP) forms of both, on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [62bf3cd](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/62bf3cd41d48b55a86151f2799b73e870f6c3dee)

- **作者**: Mingyang Wang
- **时间**: 2026-11-09T06:12:39Z
- **提交信息**: perf(attention): group tiny-KV FP8 context for uniform Q1-3 (#9018)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The tiny-KV optimization added in #8736 only admitted BF16 Q/KV and two
query tokens. FP8-E4M3 Q/KV with BF16 output therefore continued to use
the Context path, whose latency grows sharply with batch size for the
workload in #7965.

Extend the existing grouped route to equal BF16 or FP8-E4M3 Q/KV with
BF16 output and uniform query lengths 1, 2, or 3. Keep the SM103, batch
4–256, declared KV length 1–32, 16:1 query/KV heads, head dimension 128,
page size 128, packed HND layout, and existing feature/stride
restrictions. Preserve Context workspace and no-split behavior; excluded
inputs retain their existing dispatch.

B300 SM103 / CUDA 13.0 measurements for FP8 Q/KV → BF16, Q2/KV2, H16:1,
D128, page128, causal attention and PDL enabled:

| Batch | Native before → after (µs) | Speedup | Wrapper before → after
(µs) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 | 6.337 → 5.543 | 1.14× | 6.327 → 5.533 | 1.14× |
| 16 | 8.554 → 5.539 | 1.54× | 8.548 → 5.538 | 1.54× |
| 24 | 10.971 → 5.588 | 1.96× | 10.943 → 5.578 | 1.96× |
| 32 | 13.008 → 5.595 | 2.32× | 13.012 → 5.599 | 2.32× |
| 48 | 17.642 → 5.687 | 3.10× | 17.648 → 5.694 | 3.10× |
| 64 | 21.538 → 5.811 | 3.71× | 21.570 → 5.683 | 3.80× |

Matched baseline–candidate–candidate–baseline runs compare the unchanged
Context launcher at `e9735b0239f834fa2f46a633e7ab76be49a2cc06` with this
patch, using identical represented FP8 inputs, unit scales, preallocated
output/workspace/counters and separate JIT caches. Warm CUDA graphs
contain 100 calls; each run uses three rounds of ten CUDA-event samples,
excluding allocation, wrapper planning and JIT warmup. Row order is
reversed in the latter pair. Values are aggregate medians; all twelve
rows exceed the predefined 0.3 µs and 5% improvement margins. Actual
kernel traces confirm grouped dispatch, including the separate Q3 kernel
family.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Related to https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/7965,
especially [the FP8
reproducer](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/7965#issuecomment-6693101267).
Follow-up to https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8736.
Exact GB300 confirmation remains pending; this PR does not close the
issue.
